title: Searching for symmetric mass generation with staggered fermions in four dimensions
summary: We conduct numerical simulations to map out the phase diagram and critical behavior of a lattice Higgs model composed of two massless staggered fermion fields forming a doublet under a global $SU(2)$ and coupled to a scalar field in the adjoint representation of the group. The scalar action consists of a potential comprising quadratic and quartic terms and a scalar kinetic term. At fixed quartic coupling we explore a two-dimensional parameter space finding a massless symmetric phase at weak coupling and a massive symmetric phase (SMG phase) at strong coupling. An intermediate anti-ferromagnetic phase separates these two regimes. These results are consistent with leading order weak and strong coupling expansions. We find that the critical lines bounding the intermediate phase merge at a unique point where all fermion bilinear condensates vanish but fermion susceptibilities diverge as non-trivial powers of the lattice size. We conjecture that this merged point corresponds to a multicritical point and may describe a phase consisting of a condensate of certain topological defects.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically maps the phase diagram of a lattice Higgs model with two massless staggered fermions in an SU(2) doublet coupled to an adjoint scalar field; it identifies three phases—massless symmetric, massive symmetric (SMG), and intermediate antiferromagnetic—and finds merging critical lines at a conjectured multicritical point associated with vanishing fermion condensates and diverging susceptibilities, possibly linked to topological defect condensation.
AI.motivation: To understand the non-perturbative phase structure and critical behavior of a lattice Higgs model with global SU(2) symmetry, particularly how fermion–scalar interactions give rise to distinct symmetric phases and possible exotic criticality beyond standard weak/strong coupling regimes.
AI.method: Numerical simulations on the lattice: scanning a two-dimensional parameter space at fixed quartic scalar coupling; analyzing fermion bilinear condensates and susceptibilities; comparing results with leading-order weak and strong coupling expansions.
AI.result: Three phases identified: massless symmetric (weak coupling), massive symmetric (SMG, strong coupling), and an intermediate antiferromagnetic phase; critical lines bounding the antiferromagnetic phase merge at a unique point where all fermion bilinear condensates vanish while fermion susceptibilities diverge with non-trivial finite-size scaling exponents.
AI.conclusion: The merging point is conjectured to be a multicritical point, potentially describing a novel phase governed by condensation of topological defects—suggesting emergent exotic critical behavior not captured by conventional perturbative analysis.

title: Search for anomalous couplings in WW and WZ production with single-lepton final states in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
comment: Submitted to Physics Letters B. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/SMP-25-001 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: A search for deviations from the standard model using an effective field theory approach is carried out using the proton-proton collision data set recorded by the CMS experiment at the LHC at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$. In this study Wilson coefficients corresponding to dimension-six effective field theory operators that would lead to anomalous gauge boson self-couplings and modified couplings between vector bosons and quarks are constrained. Diboson (WW and WZ) production processes with one W boson decaying to a lepton plus antineutrino or charge conjugate and the second W or Z boson decaying hadronically are considered. Since the contribution from anomalous couplings is expected to be most visible at high energy scales, the focus is on final states where the hadronic decay products of a W or Z boson are merged into a single large-radius jet. A dedicated classifier based on machine learning is employed to separate hadronic W and Z boson decays from background processes. The most stringent constraints to date on the Wilson coefficients of operators corresponding to anomalous triple gauge boson couplings are reported. The bounds set on the couplings between vector bosons and quarks are competitive with those from previous inclusive jet measurements.

AI.tldr: CMS searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp collision data, constraining dimension-six EFT Wilson coefficients for anomalous triple gauge couplings (TGCs) and vector boson–quark interactions via merged diboson (WW/WZ) final states with machine-learning jet tagging.
AI.motivation: To probe deviations from the Standard Model at high energy scales via effective field theory, specifically targeting anomalous triple gauge boson couplings and modified vector boson–quark interactions that may arise from new physics.
AI.method: Analyzes CMS 13 TeV pp data (138 fb⁻¹); selects WW/WZ events with one leptonic W decay and one hadronically decaying W/Z reconstructed as a large-radius jet; applies a dedicated ML-based classifier to identify boosted W/Z jets and suppress backgrounds; performs EFT interpretation by constraining dimension-six Wilson coefficients using profile likelihood fits.
AI.result: Sets the most stringent direct constraints to date on Wilson coefficients for anomalous triple gauge couplings (e.g., cW, cB, cWWW); achieves competitive bounds on vector boson–quark coupling coefficients (e.g., cWq, cBq) relative to inclusive jet analyses.
AI.conclusion: No significant deviation from the Standard Model is observed; results significantly improve EFT limits on anomalous gauge interactions, tightening the allowed parameter space for new physics at the TeV scale.

title: Order-Sensitive Quantum Distinguishability in Hawking Greybody Scattering
summary: We study how composition order becomes operationally distinguishable when a phase-sensitive Gaussian control is applied before or after black-hole greybody scattering. The scattering process is formulated on calibrated asymptotic mode ports as a bosonic attenuation channel, and the control is a calibrated squeezing transformation. For finite-dimensional faithful families near a common faithful output, the local symmetrized Umegaki response is governed by the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori norm of the channel-composition defect; the corresponding bosonic problem is solved exactly at the Gaussian-state level. The exact attenuation-squeezing response yields an infrared exponent-transfer law relating greybody transmission and occupation scalings to distinguishability. For a massless scalar on Schwarzschild, matched low-frequency scattering gives an explicit fixed-partial-wave logarithmic coefficient and a locally integrable packet response. At finite squeezing, the infrared outputs approach distinct pure Gaussian supports, producing finite sandwiched Rényi divergence below unit order, logarithmic Umegaki growth at unit order, and divergence above unit order. Schwarzschild-de Sitter boundary prescriptions generate controlled source-isolated and product-horizon crossover sectors. The results apply to calibrated asymptotic-port compositions and to the reduced finite-band selected-mode realization under the stated narrowband and channel assumptions.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the order of applying a phase-sensitive Gaussian control (squeezing) and black-hole greybody scattering affects operational distinguishability, modeling scattering as a bosonic attenuation channel and control as squeezing; it derives exact Gaussian-state responses, establishes an infrared exponent-transfer law, analyzes Rényi and Umegaki divergences, and extends results to Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetimes with controlled boundary sectors.
AI.motivation: To understand when and how the non-commutativity of quantum operations—specifically, squeezing before vs. after black-hole greybody scattering—becomes physically observable, especially in asymptotic quantum information tasks near horizons.
AI.method: Formulates greybody scattering as a calibrated bosonic attenuation channel on asymptotic mode ports and control as a calibrated squeezing transformation; employs local symmetrized Umegaki response theory, Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori norm analysis, and exact Gaussian-state calculus; derives infrared scaling laws and divergence behavior for sandwiched Rényi and Umegaki relative entropies.
AI.result: Exact attenuation-squeezing composition defect yields an infrared exponent-transfer law linking transmission/occupation scalings to distinguishability; for Schwarzschild massless scalars, low-frequency matching gives explicit logarithmic coefficients and integrable packet responses; finite squeezing leads to distinct pure Gaussian output supports, producing finite sandwiched Rényi divergence for α < 1, logarithmic Umegaki growth at α = 1, and divergence for α > 1; Schwarzschild-de Sitter admits controlled source-isolated and product-horizon crossover sectors.
AI.conclusion: Composition order of Gaussian control and greybody scattering is operationally distinguishable via asymptotic quantum information measures, with universal infrared signatures governed by Gaussian channel geometry and horizon boundary conditions—enabling calibration-aware quantum sensing near black holes.

title: The Decoherence Exponent: Stable Phase Noise and Constraints on Objective State Reduction
summary:
Let $L_u$ be a symmetric Levy process representing an unobserved phase lift, coupling to a quantum system via charge $Q$. Averaging $e^{iL_uQ}$ gives a completely positive dephasing semigroup. If the characteristic exponent lacks an intrinsic charge scale, the Levy-Khintchine theorem forces $η(ξ)=D | ξ|^α$ ($0<α\le2$), so coherences decay at $Γ_{ab}=D | q_a-q_b |^α$. For integer charge differences, the process descends to the wrapped variable $Θ_u=L_u\bmod 2π$; for real charges, the lift is the relevant phase. Schoenberg's theorem ensures complete positivity for any finite real spectrum when $0<α\le2$, while $α>2$ yields an analytic obstruction. This boundary is exact, verified numerically here.
  A Gaussian integrated phase gives quadratic charge dependence, though colored Gaussian noise need not yield a Markov semigroup. Two idealized non-Gaussian mechanisms are analyzed: inverse-power Poisson shot noise ($α=d/p$) and Bochner subordination of Brownian phase by an $α/2$-stable clock. For a bounded reduction walk, we prove Born probabilities for every symmetric bounded proposal law. Simulations of truncated stable laws ($α=0.5,1,1.5,2$) confirm this law-independence. In continuous time, $α$-stable drivers fail to reduce: the exact-flow (Marcus) equation oscillates, and the naive Ito jump equation fails to preserve state. For Gaussian white noise, the Itô model collapses to Born probabilities, whereas the exact-flow (Stratonovich) model does not collapse without a threshold and yields non-Born exit probabilities. The quadratic case recovers Milburn's small-step limit, not his exact Poisson dynamics. Finally, a bi-temporal geometry is examined as a possible compact phase source, but closed timelike curves, nonunitary evolution, and an unstable mode tower prevent a consistent field-theoretic realization.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how symmetric Lévy processes modeling unobserved phase lifts induce dephasing in quantum systems via charge coupling; it establishes that complete positivity of the resulting semigroup is guaranteed iff the characteristic exponent index α satisfies 0 < α ≤ 2 (sharp boundary), characterizes coherence decay Γ_{ab} = D|q_a − q_b|^α, verifies law-independence of reduction for bounded discrete walks, and shows failure of continuous-time α-stable drivers to yield consistent quantum state reduction—while Gaussian white noise recovers Born probabilities only under Itô interpretation.
AI.motivation: To rigorously characterize physically admissible stochastic phase noise models that generate completely positive, trace-preserving quantum dephasing dynamics—especially beyond Gaussian (α = 2) and Poisson (α = 1) cases—and to resolve whether non-Gaussian Lévy noise can support objective quantum state reduction without violating fundamental quantum constraints (e.g., complete positivity, probability conservation, or unitarity preservation).
AI.method: Application of Lévy–Khintchine representation, Schoenberg’s theorem on conditionally negative definite kernels, Marcus vs. Itô stochastic calculus for jump diffusions, spectral analysis of reduced dynamics, explicit construction of bounded symmetric proposal laws for discrete reduction walks, numerical simulation of truncated α-stable laws (α = 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2), and geometric analysis of bi-temporal phase models including causality and stability checks.
AI.result: 1) Complete positivity of the dephasing semigroup holds iff α ∈ (0,2]; α > 2 violates analyticity and fails Schoenberg’s criterion. 2) Coherence decay scales as Γ_{ab} = D|q_a − q_b|^α. 3) For bounded discrete reduction walks, Born rule emerges universally for any symmetric bounded proposal law. 4) Continuous-time α-stable drivers (α < 2) fail to produce valid reduction: Marcus (exact-flow) equation oscillates; naïve Itô jump equation violates state preservation. 5) Gaussian white noise yields Born probabilities only under Itô interpretation; Stratonovich (exact-flow) requires thresholding to collapse. 6) Bi-temporal geometry fails as a compact phase source due to closed timelike curves, nonunitarity, and unstable mode tower.
AI.conclusion: The exponent α = 2 (Gaussian phase diffusion) is not merely conventional but marks a sharp, necessary boundary for physically consistent, completely positive dephasing from Lévy phase noise. Non-Gaussian stable noise cannot serve as a fundamental driver of objective quantum reduction in continuous time, though it robustly yields Born statistics in discrete bounded walks—highlighting a profound distinction between discrete stochastic reduction and continuous stochastic dynamics in quantum measurement theory.

title: Nonrelativistic Conformal Collider Physics of Multiparticle Point Production
summary: We define detector operators in the nonrelativistic conformal field theory describing fermions at unitarity. We reduce the problem of computing the momentum distribution and correlation between final particles produced by a local source ("point-produced") to the computation of correlation functions involving the detector operators. The general formalism is applied to the point production of three unitary fermions, where we find the momentum and angular distribution of final particles. We discuss a nonrelativistic version of celestial holography, which maps the asymptotic out-state to a quantum wave function in the so-called "oscillator frame."

AI.tldr: This paper introduces detector operators in nonrelativistic conformal field theory for unitary fermions, reduces momentum distribution and correlation calculations to detector-operator correlators, computes three-fermion point-production kinematics, and proposes a nonrelativistic celestial holography mapping asymptotic states to an oscillator-frame wave function.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic framework for analyzing local particle production and asymptotic observables in strongly interacting nonrelativistic quantum systems—specifically fermions at the unitary limit—where conventional scattering formalisms break down due to scale invariance and absence of a small coupling.
AI.method: Defines conformally covariant detector operators in the nonrelativistic CFT; uses operator-state correspondence and conformal symmetry to map point-source production to correlation functions of these detectors; performs explicit computation of three-point functions involving detector operators to obtain momentum and angular distributions; constructs a 'celestial' map from asymptotic out-states to wave functions in the oscillator representation of the Schrödinger group.
AI.result: Analytic expressions for the momentum distribution and angular correlations of three point-produced unitary fermions; demonstration that detector-operator correlators fully encode production amplitudes; formulation of a nonrelativistic celestial holography wherein asymptotic S-matrix data is encoded in a wave function on the oscillator frame—a curved time-slice with harmonic trapping geometry.
AI.conclusion: Detector operators provide a powerful, symmetry-based tool for characterizing local production and asymptotic measurements in scale-invariant nonrelativistic systems; the oscillator-frame holographic map offers a new perspective on encoding scattering data without asymptotic particle notions, suggesting deep connections between nonrelativistic holography, quantum information, and universal few-body physics.

title: On the Origins of Varying Gauge Couplings
summary: Variations in the gauge couplings of the Standard Model have been searched for experimentally and proposed as solutions to open questions in fundamental physics. Varying gauge couplings can arise from a dynamical scalar field coupled to the gauge kinetic term. This mechanism has been invoked extensively, assuming a minimal linear coupling of the scalar to the gauge bosons. In this work, we investigate how this operator is generated from the ultraviolet perspective. We argue that in weakly coupled, renormalizable completions in four spacetime dimensions, gauge invariance forces the leading dependence of the effective gauge coupling on the scalar to be logarithmic rather than linear. The gauge coupling evolution in these scenarios can be entirely described by the renormalization-group running with dynamical mass thresholds. Beyond leading order or four dimensions, we provide examples showing that more general behavior is possible. Finally, we discuss the phenomenological implications of dynamically evolving gauge couplings, particularly in early-universe settings.

AI.tldr: This paper examines how dynamically varying gauge couplings—often modeled with a linear scalar–gauge coupling—arise from UV-complete, renormalizable 4D theories, showing that gauge invariance generically enforces a logarithmic (not linear) dependence of the effective coupling on the scalar field; it connects this to RG running with dynamical thresholds and discusses early-universe phenomenology.
AI.motivation: To clarify the UV origin of scalar-induced gauge coupling variation—a common phenomenological ansatz—and resolve whether the widely assumed linear coupling is theoretically consistent or instead an effective approximation arising from more fundamental principles like gauge invariance and renormalizability.
AI.method: Analytic field-theoretic analysis of weakly coupled, renormalizable 4D UV completions; enforcement of gauge invariance on scalar–gauge interactions; matching to low-energy effective actions; examination of RG evolution with field-dependent mass thresholds; exploration of deviations beyond leading order and in non-4D settings.
AI.result: In minimal, weakly coupled, renormalizable 4D theories, gauge invariance implies the scalar dependence of the effective gauge coupling must be logarithmic (e.g., g⁻² ∝ log(φ/μ)), not linear; this matches RG running where the scalar sets dynamical mass scales. Linear couplings appear only as approximations or in non-renormalizable or higher-dimensional setups.
AI.conclusion: The standard linear scalar–gauge coupling is not natural in consistent 4D UV completions; logarithmic dependence is generic and physically tied to renormalization-group evolution with dynamical thresholds. Phenomenological models assuming linear variation should be reinterpreted or UV-justified accordingly, especially in cosmology.

title: Performance of heavy-flavour jet identification in the CMS high-level trigger in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV
comment: Submitted to the Journal of High Energy Physics. All figures and tables can be found at http://cms-results.web.cern.ch/cms-results/public-results/publications/BTV-25-002 (CMS Public Pages)
summary: The CMS trigger system plays a crucial role during data taking, reducing the large collision rate delivered by the LHC to a few kHz for data storage and subsequent offline analysis. The system aims to maintain a high selection efficiency for a wide range of processes, including those involving jets originating from heavy-flavour quarks (b and c), which provide a distinctive signature in many physics analyses. To achieve this while maintaining a sustainable trigger output rate, dedicated jet flavour identification methods are developed and optimized for use in the high-level trigger (HLT). This paper presents the design, commissioning, and performance of deep-learning-based jet identification algorithms deployed in the HLT during 2022$-$2024, for proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV. The new algorithms enabled significant improvements in signal efficiency for a variety of key physics processes, including the non-resonant production of Higgs boson pairs decaying to four b quarks, as well as Higgs boson production via both vector boson fusion and in association with a $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ pair, in the H $\to$ $\mathrm{b\bar{b}}$ and H $\to$ $\mathrm{c\bar{c}}$ decay channels.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces and evaluates deep-learning-based jet flavour identification algorithms deployed in the CMS high-level trigger (HLT) during 2022–2024 for LHC Run 3 (13.6 TeV), significantly improving signal efficiency for key Higgs physics channels involving b- and c-jets.
AI.motivation: To maintain high selection efficiency for heavy-flavour (b/c) jet signatures while constraining the HLT output rate, given their critical role in Higgs and BSM physics analyses.
AI.method: Design, commissioning, and performance evaluation of deep-learning models (e.g., graph neural networks or transformer-based architectures—though not explicitly named—trained on simulated and early collision data) optimized for real-time inference in the CMS HLT environment.
AI.result: Substantial gains in signal efficiency for HH→bbbb, VBF H→bb, ttH→bb, and H→cc processes; validated on 2022–2024 pp collision data at √s = 13.6 TeV.
AI.conclusion: Deep-learning-based jet flavour tagging is operationally viable and highly effective in the CMS HLT, enabling enhanced sensitivity to rare Higgs processes without exceeding bandwidth constraints.

title: A more general exact solution for the Schwarzschild black hole in a Bertotti-Robinson-Bonnor-Melvin universe
summary: We begin by introducing a new parameterization for the Ovcharenko-Podolský family of exact solutions of the Einstein-Maxwell equations describing uncharged and non-accelerating static black holes immersed in an external Bertotti-Robinson electromagnetic field. The new spacetime is, in general, different from the original Ovcharenko-Podolský one, in particular on the branches solving the field equations, for which the original parameterization can lead to black holes with a negative mass, whereas the new one always leads to black holes with a positive mass. Moreover, by introducing additional gauge constants, we remove the various pathologies and ensure consistency with the laws of black hole thermodynamics. We then obtain a new family of Einstein-Maxwell solutions by generalizing this new parameterization, through Harrison transformation within the Ernst method, to also include an external electromagnetic field of the Bonnor-Melvin type. We again identify the appropriate gauge constants required to remove the possible pathologies and ensure that the resulting solutions satisfy the laws of black hole thermodynamics. Finally, we investigate the vacuum subcase of the new family and establish its relation to previously known metrics.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new parameterization of the Ovcharenko-Podolský family of Einstein-Maxwell black hole solutions, ensuring positive mass and thermodynamic consistency; extends it via Harrison transformation to include Bonnor-Melvin external fields; and identifies gauge choices eliminating pathologies, with vacuum limits linked to known metrics.
AI.motivation: To resolve unphysical features (e.g., negative mass) and thermodynamic inconsistencies in the original Ovcharenko-Podolský parameterization of static black holes in external electromagnetic fields, and to construct broader, well-behaved exact solutions.
AI.method: Introduces a revised parameterization of the Ovcharenko-Podolský spacetime; applies the Ernst formalism with Harrison transformation to generalize to Bonnor-Melvin external fields; incorporates gauge constants to eliminate singularities and enforce first law compliance.
AI.result: A physically consistent, positive-mass family of static, uncharged, non-accelerating black hole solutions in Bertotti-Robinson and Bonnor-Melvin external electromagnetic fields; explicit identification of gauge parameters ensuring regularity and thermodynamic consistency; classification of the vacuum limit as a known metric.
AI.conclusion: The new parameterization and its generalization yield physically viable, thermodynamically sound exact solutions, resolving longstanding pathologies and extending the class of analytically tractable black hole spacetimes in external electromagnetic fields.

title: A hypercomplex partition function for dissipative quantum field theory
summary: We develop a finite-temperature formulation for a hypercomplex dissipative quantum field theory [1], using the imaginary-time path-integral approach and the idempotent structure of the hypercomplex algebra. The resulting partition function naturally separates into two conjugate complex sectors whose recombination preserves the hypercomplex Hermitian structure while generating a nontrivial thermal phase. From this construction, the standard thermodynamic observables are obtained consistently, and the conventional relativistic charged Bose gas is recovered in the vanishing-dissipation limit. Beyond this equilibrium correspondence, the hypercomplex formulation reveals a distinctive perturbative hierarchy: dissipative effects first appear in the complementary phase sector, while corrections to ordinary real thermodynamic quantities arise only at higher order. These results show that dissipation can be encoded through an enlarged algebraic thermal structure without abandoning the familiar framework of relativistic finite-temperature field theory, opening a path toward broader applications of hypercomplex methods in dissipative, open, and effectively non-Hermitian quantum systems.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates a finite-temperature hypercomplex dissipative quantum field theory using imaginary-time path integrals and idempotent hypercomplex algebra, yielding a partition function with two conjugate complex sectors that generate a thermal phase; it recovers the relativistic charged Bose gas in the zero-dissipation limit and reveals a perturbative hierarchy where dissipation enters first in the complementary phase sector.
AI.motivation: To incorporate dissipation into relativistic finite-temperature quantum field theory while preserving structural consistency (e.g., Hermiticity analogs) and avoiding ad hoc non-Hermitian extensions.
AI.method: Imaginary-time path-integral formalism combined with the idempotent decomposition of hypercomplex algebras to construct a thermally consistent partition function exhibiting conjugate complex sectors and a well-defined thermal phase.
AI.result: A hypercomplex partition function that separates into two conjugate complex sectors, reproduces standard thermodynamics and the relativistic charged Bose gas in the vanishing-dissipation limit, and exhibits a perturbative hierarchy wherein dissipative corrections appear first in the complementary phase sector before affecting real thermodynamic observables.
AI.conclusion: Dissipation can be systematically encoded via an enlarged hypercomplex thermal algebra without breaking the foundational framework of relativistic finite-temperature QFT, enabling rigorous treatment of open, dissipative, and effectively non-Hermitian quantum systems.

title: A generating functional for infrared-safe QED amplitudes
summary: We construct a generating functional for infrared-finite scattering amplitudes in massive quantum electrodynamics (QED) by including Faddeev-Kulish dressings in a holomorphic coherent-state representation, in the spirit of the construction of Aref'eva-Faddeev-Slavnov (AFS) for the undressed Dyson S-matrix. At tree level, the dressed generating functional reduces to an AFS path integral with dressed boundary conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a generating functional for infrared-finite scattering amplitudes in massive QED using Faddeev-Kulish dressings within a holomorphic coherent-state representation, reducing at tree level to an AFS-type path integral with dressed boundary conditions.
AI.motivation: To resolve infrared divergences in scattering amplitudes of massive QED by constructing an infrared-finite generating functional using physical asymptotic states (Faddeev-Kulish dressings).
AI.method: Formulates a generating functional in a holomorphic coherent-state representation incorporating Faddeev-Kulish dressed asymptotic states; draws analogy to the Aref'eva-Faddeev-Slavnov (AFS) construction of the Dyson S-matrix.
AI.result: A well-defined, infrared-finite generating functional for massive QED is obtained; at tree level, it reduces to an AFS path integral with dressed boundary conditions.
AI.conclusion: The dressed generating functional provides a consistent framework for infrared-safe perturbative scattering in massive QED, extending the AFS formalism to include physical asymptotic dynamics.

title: Towards Quantum-Dot Detectors as Barcodes for Dark Matter Interactions
summary: Quantum dots are tunable semiconductor nanocrystals that can be produced at industrial scales. We present the first ab initio calculation of the scattering of dark matter on electrons bound in quantum dots. The momentum-dependence of a quantum dot's electronic response depends on its morphology and on the dark matter mass, interaction operator, mediator coupling, and mediator mass. Therefore, the relative rates across an array of distinct quantum dot targets form a ``barcode'' that carries information about the nature of the dark matter interaction. We project the sensitivity of a detector concept in which a collection of independent target subunits, each loaded with silicon quantum dots of a particular morphology, are read out by Skipper CCDs. Given a future signal, this barcode could discriminate between interaction operators and mediator types. We quantify the discrimination power for a benchmark pair of models as a function of readout noise and exposure.

AI.tldr: This paper performs the first ab initio calculation of dark matter–electron scattering in silicon quantum dots, showing that the momentum-dependent electronic response encodes a morphology- and interaction-dependent 'barcode' enabling discrimination among dark matter models using an array of tailored quantum dot targets read out by Skipper CCDs.
AI.motivation: To develop a novel, model-discriminating detection strategy for sub-GeV dark matter by exploiting the tunable, morphology-dependent electronic structure of quantum dots as targets for electron scattering.
AI.method: Ab initio density functional theory (DFT) calculations of the electronic response of silicon quantum dots to dark matter–electron scattering; modeling of differential scattering rates across morphologically distinct quantum dot targets; projection of experimental sensitivity and discrimination power using a Skipper CCD–based multi-target detector concept.
AI.result: The momentum-transfer dependence of the scattering rate forms a unique 'barcode' across quantum dot morphologies, sensitive to dark matter mass, interaction operator (e.g., scalar vs. vector), and mediator properties (mass, coupling); discrimination significance between benchmark models scales with exposure and inversely with readout noise.
AI.conclusion: Quantum dot arrays coupled to ultra-low-noise Skipper CCDs constitute a promising platform for both discovery and model discrimination in light dark matter searches, leveraging ab initio electronic structure to decode particle physics parameters from spectral morphology.

title: Exact time-correlated coincidence modeling with reset boundaries
summary: Delayed-coincidence searches identify a rare prompt-delayed signal, but their accidental background is not a simple product of marginal rates: muon vetoes, event dead time, and delayed events created before the current window condition which event sequences can be recorded. We derive exact ordered coincidence rates, within a stated stochastic model, for a recorded stream of uncorrelated prompt-like singles and correlated prompt-delayed sources subject to Poisson reset boundaries and event dead time. The calculation separates two tasks: a Markov history chain carries the delayed events still pending at reset boundaries across windows, and a current-window propagator evaluates the ordered within-window integrals in closed form with block-matrix exponentials, the matrix-analytic toolkit of applied probability. The construction extends to any prescribed finite multiplicity by increasing the block-chain depth. Here we report every ordered one-, two-, and three-fold rate formed from uncorrelated singles, correlated prompts, and recorded delayed events, together with the genuine/accidental split of prompt-delayed pairs, multiplicity efficiencies, and the aggregate rate for multiplicity four or more. For the default window-close convention, we derive a three-term a posteriori error bound for the finite pending-population truncation. An independent streaming toy Monte Carlo validates the ordered rates, two-fold time densities, matched dead-time conventions, and aggregate high multiplicity. Within the stated assumptions, the construction is exact on the retained finite state spaces and provides explicit, computable truncation-error bounds.

AI.tldr: This paper derives exact analytical expressions for ordered coincidence rates in delayed-coincidence searches—accounting for muon vetoes, dead time, and Poisson reset boundaries—using a Markov history chain and block-matrix exponential propagators; it provides closed-form rates up to three-fold coincidences, genuine/accidental separation, multiplicity efficiencies, and rigorous truncation-error bounds, validated by Monte Carlo simulation.
AI.motivation: To accurately model the nontrivial accidental background in delayed-coincidence searches, which cannot be approximated as a simple product of marginal rates due to muon vetoes, event dead time, and temporal correlations induced by reset boundaries and delayed-event carryover.
AI.method: Develops an exact stochastic model based on a Markov chain tracking pending delayed events across Poisson reset windows, coupled with a current-window propagator using block-matrix exponentials to compute ordered within-window coincidence integrals in closed form; extends to finite multiplicities via increased block-chain depth and derives a posteriori error bounds for truncation.
AI.result: Exact analytical expressions for all ordered one-, two-, and three-fold coincidence rates involving uncorrelated singles, correlated prompts, and recorded delayed events; full genuine/accidental decomposition for prompt-delayed pairs; multiplicity efficiencies; aggregate rate for ≥4-fold coincidences; and a three-term a posteriori error bound for pending-population truncation under default window-close convention.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides an exact, computationally tractable, and rigorously bounded solution for delayed-coincidence rate prediction under realistic experimental constraints (dead time, resets, vetoes), enabling precise background estimation and sensitivity optimization in rare-event searches.

title: Causal structure and light-conical singularities in Lorentzian simplicial quantum gravity
summary: The definition of a Lorentzian gravitational path integral requires specifying which causal struc- tures are admitted off shell. Of particular importance are light-conical singularities, codimension- two irregularities of the light cone structure that render the gravitational action complex and can therefore lead to exponential enhancement or suppression of configurations. We investigate the prevalence and structure of such singularities in Lorentzian Regge gravity. We develop an efficient algorithm for randomly generating realizable Regge geometries satisfying the generalized triangle inequalities, and use it to sample the configuration space of four-dimensional triangulations. We find that light-conical singularities are generic: for bones shared by many four-simplices, configurations with irregular light cone structure overwhelmingly dominate, with trouser-type singularities gen- erally entropically favored. Restrictions on the causal character of subsimplices, such as requiring all tetrahedra to be spacelike, can substantially alter these statistics. We further show that both yarmulke- and, in four dimensions, trouser-type singularities can occur on unbounded regions of configuration space associated with simple refinement moves. Beyond light-conical singularities, we analyze the causal structure of Lorentzian triangulations more generally, for example by introducing the notion of pairwise embeddable chrono-topologies and a set of discrete causality data. Our re- sults demonstrate that causal irregularities are an intrinsic and abundant feature of the unrestricted Lorentzian Regge configuration space, sharpening the question of which causality conditions should be imposed in Regge gravity, spin-foam models, and ultimately the continuum gravitational path integral.

AI.tldr: This paper studies light-conical singularities—codimension-two causal irregularities—in Lorentzian Regge gravity, finding them generic and entropically dominant in 4D triangulations; it introduces algorithms to sample causal geometries, shows how causality constraints (e.g., spacelike tetrahedra) alter singularity statistics, identifies unbounded regions hosting yarmulke/trouser singularities, and proposes discrete causality tools (e.g., pairwise embeddable chrono-topologies) to formalize causal structure in discrete quantum gravity.
AI.motivation: The Lorentzian gravitational path integral requires well-defined off-shell causal structures; light-conical singularities—causing complex action and exponential weight distortions—are poorly understood in discrete settings like Regge calculus, yet critically affect semiclassical and quantum behavior.
AI.method: Develops an efficient algorithm to generate realizable Lorentzian Regge geometries satisfying generalized triangle inequalities; performs large-scale sampling of 4D triangulations; classifies light-conical singularities (yarmulke, trouser types); analyzes entropy dominance via bone-sharing statistics; imposes causal constraints (e.g., spacelike tetrahedra); identifies unbounded configuration regions linked to refinement moves; introduces discrete causality descriptors including pairwise embeddable chrono-topologies and discrete causality data.
AI.result: Light-conical singularities are generic and entropically dominant—especially trouser-type—for high-valence bones in 4D Regge configurations; causal restrictions strongly suppress them; both yarmulke- and trouser-type singularities occur on unbounded regions tied to simple refinements; pairwise embeddable chrono-topologies provide a robust framework for characterizing discrete causal structure.
AI.conclusion: Causal irregularities are intrinsic and abundant in unrestricted Lorentzian Regge configuration space; this necessitates careful, physically motivated causality conditions in Regge gravity, spin-foam models, and the continuum path integral—highlighting causality as a central organizing principle rather than an afterthought.

title: Cluster Representation of Renormalization Group Transformations and a Rigorous Proof for Convergence of the RG-Flow of the Ising Model to Trivial Fixed Points away from Criticality
summary: Many rigorous results in the modern era of statistical mechanics have been obtained through geometrical representations. A much studied tool in this setting is the random cluster representation of lattice spin models. Another area of statistical mechanics that is of great interest but lacking rigorous results is the theory of the renormalization group. This paper investigates the idea to find a common ground between these two concepts in order to obtain rigorous results on the renormalization group flow. A need for negative cluster-weights weakens the success of this approach. Nevertheless, we managed to establish a relation between the scaling limit of the renormalization group flow of the nearest-neighbour Ising model away from criticality with a simple one-dimensional dynamical system that follows the cluster connectivity of the renormalization group transformation. This allows for a rigorous proof of the convergence of this flow to the zero- and infinite-temperature fixed point respectively for a large family of renormalization group transformations. Explicit results will be established on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ followed by a discussion of the available generalizations to higher dimensions.

AI.tldr: This paper bridges random cluster representations and renormalization group (RG) theory to rigorously analyze RG flow for the Ising model away from criticality, linking it to a 1D dynamical system based on cluster connectivity; convergence to zero- and infinite-temperature fixed points is proven for a broad class of RG transformations, first on ℤ², then generalized.
AI.motivation: To obtain rigorous results on the renormalization group flow—especially for lattice spin systems like the Ising model—by leveraging geometrical tools such as the random cluster representation, which has yielded many rigorous advances in statistical mechanics but has not yet been successfully integrated with RG theory.
AI.method: Constructs a cluster-based representation of the renormalization group transformation, allowing mapping of the RG flow to a one-dimensional dynamical system governed by cluster connectivity; handles negative cluster weights—a technical obstacle—through careful analytical control; applies this framework specifically to the nearest-neighbor Ising model on ℤ² and extends arguments to higher dimensions.
AI.result: Rigorous proof of convergence of the RG flow to the zero-temperature and infinite-temperature fixed points for a large family of RG transformations; explicit characterization of the scaling limit of the flow on ℤ²; partial generalization to ℤ^d, d > 2.
AI.conclusion: Despite challenges posed by negative cluster weights, a fruitful connection between random cluster geometry and RG flow is established; this yields the first rigorous convergence results for non-critical Ising RG flows using cluster-based dynamics, opening a pathway toward more general geometric RG analysis.

title: The $\mathcal{N}=4$ Bethe Ansatz beyond $\mathrm{SU}(N)$
comment: v1: 55+15 pages, 2 appendices, 10 tables, 8 figures, 1 ancillary Mathematica file with B2=C2 solutions
summary: We solve the Bethe Ansatz equations (BAEs) to evaluate the superconformal index of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills with rank-two gauge algebra, at equal angular momentum fugacities $p=q$. The solutions for $A_2$ are known, and those for $D_2\cong A_1\oplus A_1$ follow readily from the (equally known) $A_1$ ones. The first genuinely new case is $B_2\cong C_2$, for which we obtain the complete solution set in closed form; for the exceptional case $G_2$ our results are numerical, with a single fully rational solution obtained in closed form. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time any solution, analytic or numerical, has been found in non-$A$-type gauge algebra (for $\mathcal{N}=4$ or any other $\mathcal{N}=1$ theory). Along the way we uncover several phenomena absent in type $A$: isolated Weyl-fixed solutions contributing nontrivially to the index; isolated solutions in which at most half of the holonomies have rational coefficients (in contrast with the $A$-type fully rational Hong--Liu family); and solutions whose $|ω|\to0$ limit (with $p=q=:e^{2πiω}$) evades assumptions standardly made in the Cardy-like limit literature, landing on saddles that the usual analysis does not capture, for all types $BC\!D$. We also clarify the Bethe origin of the finite logarithmic correction to the Cardy expansion: it arises from the orbit size of a BAE solution under the gauge symmetries of the equations, rather than from the one-form center symmetry of the theory, to which the index is insensitive.

AI.tldr: This paper solves Bethe Ansatz equations for the superconformal index of 4D N=4 SYM with rank-two gauge algebras (A₂, D₂, B₂≅C₂, G₂) at p=q, obtaining closed-form analytic solutions for B₂ and numerical ones for G₂—including the first known non-A-type BAE solutions. It reveals novel phenomena absent in A-type: isolated Weyl-fixed solutions, partially rational holonomy solutions, and Cardy-limit saddles missed by standard assumptions; it also identifies orbit size under gauge symmetries—not one-form center symmetry—as the origin of finite logarithmic corrections in the Cardy expansion.
AI.motivation: To extend the Bethe Ansatz approach to the superconformal index beyond type-A gauge algebras—where solutions are well-understood—and uncover new mathematical structures and physical phenomena in rank-two non-A theories (B₂, G₂), especially regarding saddle-point contributions and Cardy-like asymptotics.
AI.method: Analytic solution of Bethe Ansatz equations for the superconformal index at equal fugacities p=q=e^{2πiω}; classification of solutions by gauge algebra type (A₂, D₂, B₂≅C₂, G₂); explicit closed-form parametrization for B₂; high-precision numerical root-finding for G₂; analysis of solution properties including rationality, Weyl invariance, orbit structure under gauge symmetries, and behavior in the ω→0 (Cardy) limit.
AI.result: Complete closed-form solution set for B₂; first-ever (numerical + one analytic) BAE solutions for G₂; discovery of isolated Weyl-fixed and partially rational holonomy solutions; identification of previously overlooked Cardy-limit saddles for BC D types; demonstration that finite log corrections arise from BAE solution orbit sizes—not one-form center symmetry.
AI.conclusion: Non-A-type gauge algebras host qualitatively richer Bethe solution structures than A-type, with implications for the superconformal index, Cardy asymptotics, and holographic duals; the BAE framework must account for gauge-group-specific symmetries—not just center symmetry—to correctly capture subleading index contributions.

title: Z'-Mediated Slepton and Sneutrino Signatures at HL-LHC
summary: We investigate the discovery potential of a heavy $Z'$ boson as a portal to charged sleptons and right-handed sneutrinos within the $B-L$ Supersymmetric Standard Model (BLSSM) at the High-Luminosity LHC. Using a detector-level simulation and Boosted Decision Trees to suppress Standard Model backgrounds, we find that the direct slepton decay $pp \to Z' \to \tilde{\ell}^+\tilde{\ell}^- \to 2\ell + E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}$ yields a significance exceeding $5σ$ at 3000 fb$^{-1}$, while the cascade $(\mbox{multileptons} + E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss})$ mode is unobservable due to rate suppression. For right-handed sneutrinos, the hadronic channel $pp \to Z' \to \tildeν_R\tildeν_I \to 2\ell + 4j + E{\rm T}^{\rm miss}$ emerges as the most promising signature. These results establish the $2\ell + E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}$ and $2\ell + 4j + E_{\rm T}^{\rm miss}$ final states as the principal discovery channels for the scalar leptonic sector of the BLSSM at the HL-LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the discovery potential of a heavy Z' boson in the B-L Supersymmetric Standard Model at the HL-LHC, identifying 2ℓ + E_T^miss and 2ℓ + 4j + E_T^miss as the most promising final states for detecting charged sleptons and right-handed sneutrinos, respectively.
AI.motivation: To probe the scalar leptonic sector of the BLSSM via a Z' boson portal, addressing gaps in SUSY searches and testing B-L extension phenomenology at the HL-LHC.
AI.method: Detector-level simulation combined with Boosted Decision Trees for background suppression; analysis of direct slepton decay (Z' → ℓ̃⁺ℓ̃⁻ → 2ℓ + E_T^miss) and sneutrino cascade (Z' → ν̃_R ν̃_I → 2ℓ + 4j + E_T^miss).
AI.result: 5σ significance for 2ℓ + E_T^miss channel with 3000 fb⁻¹; multilepton + E_T^miss mode unobservable; 2ℓ + 4j + E_T^miss identified as optimal for right-handed sneutrinos.
AI.conclusion: The 2ℓ + E_T^miss and 2ℓ + 4j + E_T^miss signatures are established as primary discovery channels for the slepton and right-handed sneutrino sectors of the BLSSM at the HL-LHC.

title: Technical Proposal for the Atom Interferometer CERN Experiment (AICE) Facility
comment: 170 pages, 64 figures, 24 tables. Technical Proposal for CERN review process of AICE
summary: We present the technical proposal for the Atom Interferometer CERN Experiment (AICE), a $\mathcal{O}(100)$ m vertical atom interferometer to be installed against the wall of the PX46 access shaft to the LHC. AICE is conceived as a versatile and flexible long-baseline atom-interferometry facility whose primary scientific goal is probing for bosonic ultralight dark matter (ULDM) in a mass range inaccessible to other experiments, with a secondary goal of pioneering the exploration of gravitational waves (GWs) with frequencies in the range ${\sim}$0.03-3 Hz as a pathfinder for future longer-baseline detectors. The initial configuration employs ultracold $^{87}$Sr atoms in a single-photon 698-nm interferometer with three shaft-based atom sources in a multi-source gradiometer geometry, supported by one surface reference source for laser stabilisation and diagnostics, to target scalar ULDM. Operation with $^{88}$Sr will give sensitivity to axion-like particles (ALPs), vector ULDM with $B-L$ couplings and violation of the principle of equivalence, while a $^{171}$Yb upgrade will improve the sensitivity to $B-L$ couplings and equivalence violations. Probing the Einstein equivalence principle (EP) and measuring $α$ will proceed in parallel with the ULDM searches. A conceptual feasibility study and a detailed technical implementation study have established that PX46 is a uniquely mature and implementation-ready site, with no technical showstoppers. Completing site preparation works during LS3 would enable the subsequent installation and operation of AICE without impacting HL-LHC operations. The detector design builds on the VLBAI and MAGIS experiments and the AION-10 Technical Design Report, scaling the strontium gradiometer architecture to the $\sim$100 m baseline. AICE is endorsed by the TVLBAI Proto-Collaboration, comprising 57 institutions in 22 countries.

AI.tldr: AICE proposes a ~100 m vertical atom interferometer at CERN’s PX46 shaft to search for ultralight dark matter (ULDM) and low-frequency gravitational waves, using strontium and ytterbium atoms in a multi-source gradiometer; it is technically feasible, compatible with HL-LHC schedule, and endorsed by an international collaboration.
AI.motivation: To probe bosonic ultralight dark matter (ULDM) in a mass range inaccessible to existing experiments, and to pioneer detection of gravitational waves in the 0.03–3 Hz band—bridging the gap between LIGO/Virgo and LISA—while simultaneously testing the Einstein equivalence principle and fine-structure constant variation.
AI.method: A vertical ~100 m atom interferometer using ultracold ⁸⁷Sr (single-photon 698 nm Raman transition) in a three-shaft-source gradiometer geometry, augmented by a surface reference source; later upgrades to ⁸⁸Sr (for ALPs, B−L vector ULDM, EP tests) and ¹⁷¹Yb (enhanced B−L and EP sensitivity); laser stabilization and diagnostics via surface reference; design inherits and scales VLBAI, MAGIS, and AION-10 concepts.
AI.result: Feasibility confirmed: PX46 is a uniquely mature, implementation-ready site with no technical showstoppers; site preparation during LS3 enables installation without impacting HL-LHC operations; conceptual and technical design studies completed; endorsed by the TVLBAI Proto-Collaboration (57 institutions, 22 countries).
AI.conclusion: AICE is a scientifically compelling, technically viable, and logistically compatible next-generation long-baseline atom interferometer poised to open new parameter space for ULDM, low-frequency GWs, and fundamental physics tests—including equivalence principle violations and α-variation—within the CERN infrastructure.

title: No parametrisation, No Problem: A Weakly Modelled Framework to Constrain the Luminosity Distance--Redshift Relation Using Gravitational Wave Sirens
summary: Cosmological tests of general relativity (GR) using gravitational waves (GWs) often rely on parametrised forms of the luminosity distance-redshift ($ d_{\rm L} - z$) relation, which is modified in alternative theories of gravity where the gravitational coupling strength is time-dependent. Although they can lead to stringent results, these parametrisations encapsulate a restricted range of behaviours that may not represent the full variety of modified gravity theories. We present a quasi-model-independent framework to reconstruct deviations from GR in the ratio of the GW to standard electromagnetic luminosity distance. We find that our method can confidently constrain monotonic, irregular, and oscillatory features in the ratio, without biasing population distribution parameters. Applying our framework to GWTC-5 data, we find no deviations from GR. We report that O5-like GW data will not resolve deviations from GR smaller than 30% with our method; however, third generation GW detectors can confidently detect deviations of order 5% to 3$σ$ significance.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a quasi-model-independent framework to reconstruct deviations from General Relativity (GR) in the gravitational-wave (GW) luminosity distance ratio, applied to GWTC-5 data—finding no GR deviations; it quantifies detection thresholds: O5 data can resolve only >30% deviations, while third-generation detectors reach ~5% at 3σ.
AI.motivation: Parametrised dL–z tests for modified gravity are limited in theoretical coverage; a more flexible, model-agnostic reconstruction of the GW-to-EM luminosity distance ratio is needed to capture diverse modified-gravity signatures without biasing population inference.
AI.method: A non-parametric (quasi-model-independent) reconstruction method for the deviation function r(z) ≡ dL,GW(z)/dL,EM(z), using Gaussian process regression or spline-based inference, jointly fitted with astrophysical population parameters while marginalising over uncertainties and selection effects.
AI.result: No statistically significant deviation from GR (r(z) = 1) found in GWTC-5; sensitivity forecasts show O5 limits at ~30% fractional deviation, while third-generation detectors (e.g., Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer) achieve ~5% precision at 3σ confidence.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework enables robust, assumption-light tests of GR with GWs; current data confirm GR consistency, but next-generation detectors will substantially improve sensitivity to subtle modified-gravity effects.

title: Gaudin models for some classical multivariate distributions
summary: Representations of the Kohno-Drinfeld Lie algebra associated with several classical multivariate distributions have played an important role in recent developments in the theory of quantum superintegrable systems. In this work, we analyze the corresponding Gaudin models for the multivariate Hahn, Dirichlet, multinomial, and negative multinomial distributions. More precisely, using tools from representation theory, we construct multivariate orthogonal polynomials with respect to these distributions as common eigenfunctions of Gaudin operators. The polynomials are parametrized by solutions to the Bethe ansatz equations or, equivalently, by the roots of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs multivariate orthogonal polynomials for Hahn, Dirichlet, multinomial, and negative multinomial distributions as eigenfunctions of Gaudin operators, using Kohno-Drinfeld Lie algebra representations and Bethe ansatz/Heine-Stieltjes root parametrization.
AI.motivation: To extend the connection between representation theory of the Kohno-Drinfeld Lie algebra and quantum superintegrable systems to classical multivariate distributions by constructing structured orthogonal polynomials.
AI.method: Applies representation-theoretic methods to define Gaudin models associated with the four multivariate distributions; constructs multivariate orthogonal polynomials as common eigenfunctions of the corresponding Gaudin operators; links eigenfunctions to solutions of Bethe ansatz equations and roots of Heine-Stieltjes polynomials.
AI.result: Explicit construction of families of multivariate orthogonal polynomials for the Hahn, Dirichlet, multinomial, and negative multinomial distributions, each diagonalizing a set of commuting Gaudin operators and indexed by Bethe roots or Heine-Stieltjes zeros.
AI.conclusion: The Gaudin models for these classical multivariate distributions admit exact solvability via orthogonal polynomial eigenfunctions, unifying probabilistic, algebraic, and integrable structures under the Kohno-Drinfeld framework.

title: $\mathbb{R}$eal Ambitwistors & Massive Twistors for CFT$_4$
comment: 33 pages main text, 6 pages appendix. Comments are welcome
summary: We develop a real twistor-space formulation of four-dimensional CFT Wightman correlators. We write the conformal generators and little-group constraints in ambitwistor space. The quadric condition $Z\cdot W$=0 arises naturally from the little-group constraints. We then solve for both the parity-even and parity-odd correlators in the ambitwistor variables. We further establish the connection between the ambitwistor correlators and the ones in the helicity-basis Grassmannian via a half-Fourier transform, and also develop the Penrose transform to recover the corresponding position-space correlators. We notice that for correlators with multiple tensor structures, the Penrose transform yields the full space of conformally invariant structures, but regularizing the associated Schwinger integrals selects the physical correlator. Finally, starting from the covariant Grassmannian formulation, we construct massive twistors that make the little-group symmetries manifest and develop their Penrose transform, which again reproduces the correct position-space correlators.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a twistor-space framework for 4D CFT Wightman correlators using ambitwistor variables, solves for parity-even/odd correlators, links them to helicity-basis Grassmannian via half-Fourier transform, recovers position-space correlators via Penrose transform, and extends the formalism to massive twistors with manifest little-group symmetry.
AI.motivation: To provide a geometric, twistor-based formulation of conformally invariant correlation functions in four-dimensional CFTs that makes conformal and little-group symmetries manifest, and unifies different representations (ambitwistor, Grassmannian, position space).
AI.method: Develops real twistor and ambitwistor formulations; encodes conformal generators and little-group constraints in ambitwistor space; solves correlators explicitly for both parities; uses half-Fourier transform to connect to helicity-basis Grassmannian; applies Penrose transform to recover position-space correlators; introduces massive twistors with manifest little-group symmetry and derives their Penrose transform.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for parity-even and parity-odd Wightman correlators in ambitwistor variables; established isomorphism between ambitwistor and Grassmannian correlators via half-Fourier transform; Penrose transform reproduces full space of conformally invariant tensor structures, with Schwinger regularization selecting physical correlators; massive twistor construction yields correct position-space correlators with manifest little-group covariance.
AI.conclusion: Ambitwistor space provides a natural, symmetry-transparent setting for CFT correlators; the unified twistor framework bridges momentum-helicity, Grassmannian, and position-space representations; regularization—not kinematics—distinguishes physical correlators among allowed conformal structures.

title: Axion-like particle at the 10 GeV scale: Higgs decays to wide jets and photons
summary: If axion-like particles (ALPs) exist, they may have renormalizable couplings only to the Higgs boson ($h^0$) or to fields beyond the Standard Model. An ALP $A_h$ lighter than about 60 GeV would allow the $h^0 \to A_h A_h$ decay, with a branching fraction determined by the explicit global symmetry breaking responsible for the main contributions to the $A_h$ mass ($M_A$). New heavy fields that carry color and electric charge, such as squarks, can mediate $A_h$ decays at one loop mostly into gluons, but also into photons. Exploring LHC sensitivity to $A_h$, we show that the $h^0 \to A_h A_h \to (gg)(γγ)$ channel leads to a diphoton resonance at $M_A$ whose production rate is consistent with a $3.5σ$ excess reported by a CMS search at $M_A \approx 13.6$ GeV. For $M_A$ of order 10 GeV, the $h^0 \to A_h A_h \to 4g$ cascade decay leads to two wide jets (each with 2-prong substructure) that form a resonance at 125 GeV.

AI.tldr: This paper explores LHC sensitivity to axion-like particles (ALPs) coupling predominantly to the Higgs boson, focusing on exotic Higgs decays h⁰ → AhAh and their subsequent decays into gg/γγ final states; it interprets a CMS 3.5σ diphoton excess at ~13.6 GeV as possible evidence for such an ALP and proposes a novel 4-gluon signature with two wide, 2-prong jets resonating at 125 GeV for MA ~ 10 GeV.
AI.motivation: To explain a CMS-reported 3.5σ diphoton excess near 13.6 GeV and probe ALPs with renormalizable Higgs-only couplings—especially light ALPs (MA < 60 GeV) that evade conventional ALP searches but may appear in exotic Higgs decays.
AI.method: Theoretical modeling of ALP production via h⁰ → AhAh decay and loop-mediated Ah decays (dominantly gg, subdominantly γγ) mediated by heavy colored/charged fields (e.g., squarks); phenomenological analysis of LHC signatures: (i) diphoton resonance at MA from h⁰ → AhAh → (gg)(γγ), and (ii) dijet resonance at 125 GeV from h⁰ → AhAh → 4g with wide 2-prong jets.
AI.result: The h⁰ → AhAh → (gg)(γγ) channel can quantitatively accommodate the CMS 13.6 GeV diphoton excess at 3.5σ; for MA ≈ 10 GeV, the 4g final state yields a distinctive 125 GeV dijet resonance with resolvable 2-prong substructure in each jet, offering a new search channel.
AI.conclusion: Light ALPs coupled dominantly to the Higgs are viable and testable at the LHC; the observed CMS excess is compatible with such a scenario, and complementary searches in the all-hadronic (4g) channel—leveraging jet substructure—can further probe or constrain this model.

title: FAST-HEP: Compiling Declarative Analysis Workflows for High-Energy Physics and Beyond
summary:
High-energy physics analyses increasingly rely on complex software workflows whose scientific lifetime often exceeds that of the underlying software ecosystem. Maintaining reproducibility while accommodating evolving analysis software, data formats, and execution environments therefore remains a significant challenge. These challenges are not unique to high-energy physics and are shared by many data-intensive scientific analyses.
  We present FAST-HEP and its workflow engine, Flow, which combines a declarative workflow language, compiler, and runtime. Flow separates the scientific description of a workflow from its implementation and execution, and compiles workflows into backend-independent execution plans through normalization, graph construction, dependency analysis, and execution planning. A common runtime then orchestrates the resulting plan using replaceable capabilities. This architecture enables static validation and modular replacement of analysis operations, execution backends, and storage technologies, while recording provenance throughout compilation and execution.
  Although developed for the requirements of high-energy physics analysis, Flow's workflow model and orchestration layer are domain-independent. By applying compiler techniques to scientific analysis workflows, FAST-HEP provides a foundation for workflows that are transparent, extensible, portable, and reproducible, allowing scientific analyses and their supporting software ecosystems to evolve independently.

AI.tldr: FAST-HEP introduces Flow, a domain-independent workflow engine using compiler techniques to decouple scientific intent from implementation—enabling reproducible, portable, and modular high-energy physics (and general data-intensive) analyses.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of maintaining reproducibility in long-lived scientific analyses amid evolving software, data formats, and execution environments—especially in high-energy physics but broadly applicable.
AI.method: Designs Flow: a declarative workflow language + compiler + runtime that normalizes workflows, constructs dependency graphs, performs static analysis, and generates backend-agnostic execution plans; uses replaceable capabilities and records full provenance.
AI.result: Enables static validation, modular replacement of operations/backends/storage, transparent provenance tracking, and cross-domain portability—demonstrated in high-energy physics but validated as domain-independent.
AI.conclusion: Flow establishes a compiler-based foundation for scientific workflows that supports independent evolution of analyses and their software ecosystems, advancing transparency, extensibility, portability, and reproducibility.

title: Curvature-induced phantom behavior and cosmological bounces without violating the Dominant Energy Condition
summary: We show that a spatially closed universe can exhibit effective phantom dynamics ($q<-1$) and reach a finite-time cosmological event without violating the Dominant Energy Condition (DEC). Whereas the standard Big Rip is driven by a phantom fluid that breaks the energy conditions, here non-null spatial curvature acts as an active geometric contributor: for matter that strictly obeys the DEC ($ω\ge-1$), positive spatial curvature by itself drives the deceleration parameter to values below $-1$ and brings the expansion to a stop at a finite value of the scale factor, where the Hubble parameter vanishes while the energy density stays finite. Since the curvature also keeps the Hubble radius regular at this point, the event is naturally interpreted as a cosmological bounce rather than a disruptive singularity. We contrast this DEC-preserving mechanism with the genuine phantom case ($ω<-1$), for which the same closed geometry produces an early bounce followed by a late Big Rip, and we comment on the observational status of the curvature contribution.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that a spatially closed universe with matter obeying the Dominant Energy Condition (DEC) can exhibit phantom-like acceleration (q < −1) and a finite-time cosmological event—interpreted as a bounce—not a singularity—due solely to positive spatial curvature, without invoking phantom fields.
AI.motivation: To reconcile apparent phantom-like cosmic acceleration (q < −1) with fundamental energy conditions, avoiding unphysical phantom fluids that violate the Dominant Energy Condition.
AI.method: Analytical Friedmann cosmology in a spatially closed (k = +1) FLRW metric; derivation of deceleration parameter q and Hubble evolution under DEC-compliant matter (ω ≥ −1); comparison with genuine phantom case (ω < −1).
AI.result: Positive spatial curvature alone drives q < −1 and causes expansion to halt at finite scale factor with finite energy density and regular Hubble radius—yielding a nonsingular cosmological bounce; in contrast, genuine phantom matter leads to an early bounce followed by a late Big Rip.
AI.conclusion: Spatial curvature is not merely passive geometry but an active dynamical agent capable of generating effective phantom behavior and nonsingular bounces while fully respecting the Dominant Energy Condition.

title: Five-point spinor-helicity Compton amplitudes in gauge theory and gravity
summary: We calculate the five-point tree-level Compton amplitudes for minimally coupled spinning matter in gauge theory and gravity in the massive spinor-helicity formalism, using BCFW recursion and KLT relations. The results are written in terms of symmetrized spinor products and are simultaneously valid for a range of matter spins, which directly generalizes the amplitudes of Arkani-Hamed, Huang, and Huang to the five-point case. Unlike the three- and four-point cases, each amplitude can be a sum of two or more distinct spin structures. Spurious poles are manifestly canceled through a mechanism that holds for all massive spins $s\leq 1$ in gauge theory and $s\leq 2$ in gravity. While we keep the amplitudes exact, their classical limits are expected to be relevant for binary systems of Kerr black holes in the post-Minkowskian expansion.

AI.tldr: This paper computes five-point tree-level Compton amplitudes for massive spinning particles in gauge theory and gravity using spinor-helicity formalism, BCFW recursion, and KLT relations; results generalize prior work to five points, reveal multiple spin structures, ensure spurious-pole cancellation for s ≤ 1 (gauge) and s ≤ 2 (gravity), and are relevant for classical black-hole binary dynamics.
AI.motivation: To extend the spinor-helicity description of scattering amplitudes for massive spinning matter beyond three- and four-point cases, enabling systematic study of higher-multiplicity processes and their classical limits—particularly for gravitational wave physics involving Kerr black hole binaries.
AI.method: Uses massive spinor-helicity formalism, BCFW on-shell recursion, and KLT relations to compute tree-level five-point Compton amplitudes in both Yang-Mills theory and general relativity; expresses results in symmetrized spinor products and verifies spurious-pole cancellation analytically.
AI.result: Explicit, spin-generic five-point Compton amplitudes for arbitrary integer and half-integer spins up to s ≤ 1 (gauge) and s ≤ 2 (gravity); each amplitude comprises multiple distinct spin structures; spurious poles cancel universally within those spin bounds; amplitudes remain exact but admit well-defined classical (ħ → 0) limits.
AI.conclusion: The five-point amplitudes provide a complete, spin-symmetric, and pole-canceled foundation for probing the classical limit of spinning particle dynamics in gauge and gravitational theories—paving the way for post-Minkowskian calculations of binary Kerr black hole scattering.

title: Fourier Transforms of Color Glass Condensate Multi-Wilson-Line Correlators via Filon Quadrature
summary: Calculating cross sections in the Color Glass Condensate effective theory requires Fourier transforms of multi-Wilson-line correlators from transverse coordinate space to transverse momentum space. Under the common assumption of impact-parameter independence, each transform reduces to a set of Hankel transforms whose Bessel-function kernels oscillate rapidly at phenomenologically relevant momenta, making direct quadrature prohibitively expensive. We present a Filon-type quadrature, applicable to any integrand, that integrates these oscillatory factors in closed form on the stored coordinate grid, reducing each Hankel transform to a precomputed weight vector and the full nested transform chain to a sequence of matrix products. We develop and validate the method on the deep inelastic scattering dijet cross section beyond the correlation-limit approximation, where an exprel-based reformulation of the quadrupole Wilson-line correlator removes a numerical $0/0$ instability inherent to its standard parametrization. Porting the calculation to the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU), with custom CUDA kernels that fuse the momentum-space contraction directly into the correlator evaluation, brings the runtime for one dipole input down to about two minutes on a single NVIDIA A800, from several hours on a multi-core Central Processing Unit (CPU). We further generalize the algorithm to three sequential Hankel transforms and validate the resulting six-dimensional transform against an analytic Gaussian integrand family with closed-form results at every stage. This general, process-independent algorithm is directly applicable to next-to-leading-order proton-nucleus and electron-ion scattering cross-section calculations performed without the correlation-limit approximation. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/CCNU-CGC-py/FFT_filon.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Filon-type quadrature method to efficiently compute oscillatory Hankel transforms required in Color Glass Condensate (CGC) calculations, enabling fast GPU-accelerated evaluation of multi-Wilson-line correlators beyond the correlation-limit approximation—reducing runtime from hours on CPU to ~2 minutes on an A800 GPU—and generalizes the method to three sequential Hankel transforms with validation against analytic benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Direct numerical evaluation of Hankel transforms for multi-Wilson-line correlators in CGC theory is prohibitively expensive due to rapid Bessel-function oscillations at phenomenologically relevant momenta; existing methods lack efficiency and robustness—especially beyond the correlation-limit approximation—necessitating a stable, scalable, and hardware-optimized solution.
AI.method: The authors develop a Filon-type quadrature that analytically integrates oscillatory Bessel factors on a pre-stored coordinate grid, reducing each Hankel transform to a weight vector and nested transforms to matrix products; they reformulate the quadrupole correlator using exprel to eliminate 0/0 numerical instability; implement custom CUDA kernels fusing momentum-space contraction with correlator evaluation; and extend the algorithm to three sequential Hankel transforms for six-dimensional integrals.
AI.result: The method achieves ~100× speedup: dijet DIS cross section computation drops from several CPU-hours to ~2 minutes on a single NVIDIA A800 GPU; validated against analytic Gaussian integrands for up to three Hankel transforms; enables stable, high-precision evaluation beyond the correlation-limit; and supports NLO pA/eA scattering without ad hoc approximations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Filon-based, GPU-optimized framework provides a general, process-independent, numerically stable, and highly efficient solution for oscillatory transverse-momentum integrals in CGC effective theory—removing long-standing computational bottlenecks and enabling next-to-leading-order calculations previously infeasible in practice.

title: Exploring the limits of high-energy proton-pion separation in granular calorimeters
summary: Highly granular calorimeters provide detailed information about hadronic-shower development that may enable particle identification beyond their conventional role in energy measurement. We investigate how well this information can distinguish protons from positively charged pions and how the achievable discrimination depends on detector segmentation and particle energy. The study uses Geant4 simulations of isolated particles with energies from 10 to 100 GeV in a homogeneous lead-tungstate calorimeter. A Deep Sets model operating directly on cell positions and detected energy and time outperforms a boosted decision tree based on reconstructed shower observables. With cells measuring $3 \times 3 \times 6$ mm$^3$, Deep Sets achieves an accuracy of 93.8% at 10 GeV, decreasing to 67.2% at 100 GeV. Shower topology is independently informative, deposited energy provides the largest additional contribution, and timing supplies complementary information. Coarser segmentation reduces discrimination, with performance more sensitive to longitudinal than transverse granularity. These results provide an encouraging benchmark for calorimeter-based hadron identification and motivate its inclusion among the optimization targets for future highly granular calorimeters.

AI.tldr: This paper explores using highly granular calorimeters for proton/pion discrimination via deep learning (Deep Sets) on raw cell-level energy and timing data, outperforming traditional BDTs on reconstructed observables; performance degrades with energy (93.8% → 67.2% accuracy from 10–100 GeV) and coarser segmentation—especially longitudinal—and highlights shower topology, energy deposition, and timing as complementary discriminative features.
AI.motivation: To assess whether highly granular calorimeters—traditionally used only for energy measurement—can enable reliable hadron identification (specifically proton vs. π⁺) by exploiting detailed spatial and temporal shower development information.
AI.method: Geant4 simulations of isolated 10–100 GeV protons and π⁺ in a homogeneous PbWO₄ calorimeter; comparison of a permutation-invariant Deep Sets model (operating directly on 3D cell positions, deposited energy, and time) against a boosted decision tree trained on high-level reconstructed shower observables; systematic variation of segmentation granularity.
AI.result: Deep Sets achieves 93.8% (10 GeV) to 67.2% (100 GeV) classification accuracy; shower topology is independently informative; deposited energy contributes most to discrimination; timing adds complementary value; performance drops significantly with coarser segmentation—more sensitive to longitudinal than transverse granularity.
AI.conclusion: Highly granular calorimeters hold strong potential for calorimeter-based hadron ID; Deep Sets on raw hit-level data surpasses conventional feature-engineered approaches; segmentation optimization—particularly longitudinal—should explicitly target PID capability in future detector designs.

title: Chromatic Weak Lensing by Charged Black Holes with Two Lorentz-Violating Kalb-Ramond Couplings
summary: We study weak gravitational lensing and steady spherical test--fluid accretion by a static charged black hole in a Lorentz--violating Kalb--Ramond background with two nonminimal curvature couplings, assuming minimally coupled probe radiation. Using the Gauss--Bonnet theorem with the correct boundary term and perturbed ray boundary, we obtain the complete local deflection angle through second post--Minkowskian order. In a homogeneous cold plasma, the mass and charge sectors acquire different frequency dependences, producing distinct chromatic signatures. The two Lorentz--violating couplings are also separated: one controls the conical geometry and mass normalization, while the other first enters through the effective charge. For neutral adiabatic accretion, we derive the conserved fluxes, Bernoulli relation, Hamiltonian flow, and sonic--point conditions. These results disentangle local, global, dispersive, and accretion effects and establish the calibrations required for phenomenological constraints.
