AI.tldr: This paper analyzes weak gravitational lensing and spherical accretion around a static charged black hole in a Lorentz-violating Kalb–Ramond background with two nonminimal curvature couplings; it computes the light deflection angle to second post-Minkowskian order using Gauss–Bonnet theorem, identifies chromatic plasma effects separating mass/charge contributions and Lorentz-violating couplings, and derives full fluid-dynamical structure for neutral adiabatic accretion.
AI.motivation: To disentangle and calibrate local (lensing), global (topology), dispersive (plasma frequency dependence), and accretion effects in black hole spacetimes with Lorentz violation, enabling phenomenological constraints on quantum gravity-inspired modifications.
AI.method: Application of the Gauss–Bonnet theorem with perturbed ray boundary and correct boundary term to compute the weak-lensing deflection angle to second post-Minkowskian order; analytical derivation of steady spherical test-fluid accretion equations—including conserved fluxes, Bernoulli relation, Hamiltonian flow, and sonic-point conditions—for neutral adiabatic flow in the same background.
AI.result: Complete local deflection angle up to O(G²); chromatic separation of mass and charge contributions in cold plasma; distinct roles of the two Lorentz-violating couplings—one governing conical deficit and mass normalization, the other entering only via effective charge; full set of accretion equations valid in the Lorentz-violating background.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully isolates and quantifies individual physical effects—lensing geometry, dispersion, Lorentz violation, and hydrodynamics—providing calibrated theoretical tools for interpreting astrophysical observations (e.g., EHT, GRAVITY) in beyond-GR scenarios with Kalb–Ramond fields and curvature nonminimal couplings.

title: On uniqueness of non-vacuum stationary axisymmetric type D spacetime
summary: We study a family of the non-vacuum stationary axisymmetric type D metrics, where the two principal null directions are geodesic and shearfree. It is demonstrated that the conformal-to-Carter metric gives the most general form of this family, without any assumptions which are previously used by Ovcharenko and Podolský to arrive at this conclusion.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that the conformal-to-Carter metric is the most general form of non-vacuum, stationary, axisymmetric, type D spacetimes with geodesic and shear-free principal null directions—without relying on prior restrictive assumptions.
AI.motivation: To establish the most general form of non-vacuum stationary axisymmetric type D metrics with geodesic and shear-free principal null directions, removing previously imposed assumptions by Ovcharenko and Podolský.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of the algebraic and geometric structure of type D spacetimes within general relativity, leveraging the Goldberg–Sachs theorem and conformal invariance properties to derive the canonical form.
AI.result: The conformal-to-Carter metric is shown to be the unique and most general representative of the specified family of metrics.
AI.conclusion: The result confirms and extends earlier work by eliminating ad hoc assumptions, thereby strengthening the foundational classification of physically relevant exact solutions in general relativity.

title: Type IIA on Spin(7) manifolds with fluxes
summary: We initiate a systematic study of compactifications of type II string theory to two dimensions on Ricci-flat spaces with fluxes and sources. We derive universal constraints on such compactifications, and then develop type IIA compactifications on $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-holonomy spaces with bulk fluxes whose tadpole is cancelled by $\mathrm{OF1}$-planes. We derive the resulting two-dimensional $\mathcal N=(1,1)$ supergravity for a toroidal $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ orbifold, and we extend the metric and universal sectors geometrically to general compact $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ manifolds. In candidate supersymmetric Minkowski vacua, all untwisted shape modes appear in the flux scalar potential and can in principle be classically stabilised. However, in an explicit toroidal orbifold example flux quantisation together with the tadpole bound may obstruct the existence of candidate vacua supported entirely within the untwisted sector. The string-frame volume in string units is bounded by $7χ/192$, so suppressing $α'$ corrections requires $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ manifolds with large Euler characteristic.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically studies type II string theory compactifications to two dimensions on Ricci-flat spaces with fluxes and sources, focusing on type IIA on Spin(7)-holonomy manifolds with OF1-planes for tadpole cancellation; it derives the resulting 2D N=(1,1) supergravity, analyzes moduli stabilization via fluxes, identifies constraints from flux quantization and tadpoles in orbifold examples, and finds a string-frame volume bound tied to Euler characteristic for α′-suppression.
AI.motivation: To establish universal constraints and construct explicit, potentially supersymmetric 2D vacua from string theory via geometrically rich compactifications—specifically targeting Spin(7) manifolds—as a pathway to controlled low-dimensional effective theories with stabilized moduli.
AI.method: Derives general consistency conditions for 2D type II compactifications with fluxes and sources; constructs type IIA reductions on Spin(7) spaces including bulk NS–NS and R–R fluxes and orientifold OF1-planes; computes dimensional reduction to 2D N=(1,1) supergravity for toroidal Spin(7) orbifolds; extends results geometrically to smooth compact Spin(7) manifolds; analyzes flux-induced scalar potential for shape moduli stabilization; imposes flux quantization and tadpole cancellation constraints in explicit orbifold examples; derives volume bound from string-frame Einstein equation and curvature invariants.
AI.result: Obtains full 2D N=(1,1) supergravity action for Spin(7) compactifications including metric and universal sectors; shows untwisted shape moduli are generically lifted by flux potential; identifies obstruction to purely untwisted vacua in toroidal orbifolds due to combined flux quantization and tadpole bound; derives strict upper bound on string-frame volume: V_s ≤ 7χ/192 in string units.
AI.conclusion: Compactifications of type IIA string theory on Spin(7) manifolds with OF1-planes yield viable 2D N=(1,1) supergravities with partial classical moduli stabilization, but existence of fully untwisted supersymmetric Minkowski vacua is constrained by arithmetic (flux quantization) and topological (tadpole, Euler characteristic) data—highlighting tension between control (large volume, small α′) and topology (large χ).

title: Probing Sub-GeV Dark Matter with the Migdal Effect at JUNO
summary: We discuss the sensitivity of the JUNO neutrino detector to the Migdal ionization signal triggered by nuclear scattering events produced by sub-GeV weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). Exploiting JUNO's large target mass and the annual modulation effect we find that the aggregate rate from many independent and indistinguishable WIMP events in JUNO's liquid scintillator can be isolated from the total dark rate of the photomultipliers, potentially providing for spin-dependent interactions a world-leading sensitivity across the sub-GeV mass range.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates JUNO's sensitivity to Migdal ionization signals from sub-GeV WIMPs, leveraging its large target mass and annual modulation to achieve world-leading spin-dependent sensitivity in the sub-GeV mass range.
AI.motivation: To improve detection sensitivity for sub-GeV dark matter candidates—specifically weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs)—via the Migdal effect, which produces detectable ionization signals from nuclear recoils in liquid scintillator detectors.
AI.method: Analytical and phenomenological modeling of Migdal ionization rates induced by sub-GeV WIMP–nucleus scattering in JUNO’s liquid scintillator; incorporation of detector-specific backgrounds (e.g., photomultiplier dark rate) and exploitation of the annual modulation signature to enhance signal discrimination.
AI.result: JUNO can isolate the aggregate Migdal signal from multiple indistinguishable WIMP-induced nuclear scatters above background, achieving projected world-leading sensitivity for spin-dependent WIMP–nucleon interactions in the sub-GeV mass region.
AI.conclusion: JUNO is a highly competitive experiment for probing sub-GeV WIMPs via the Migdal effect, especially for spin-dependent couplings, due to its large target mass, low-energy threshold capability, and modulation-based background suppression.

title: Bounds on the Lyapunov Exponent of Circular Null Orbits in $n$-Dimensional Black-Hole Spacetimes
summary: Unstable circular null orbits provide a geometric bridge between black-hole optics, photon rings, strong gravitational lensing, and the eikonal sector of quasinormal ringing. In four-dimensional Einstein gravity, the instability rate of such orbits, measured by the Lyapunov exponent $λ$, obeys model-independent upper bounds when the matter sector satisfies standard energy conditions. We extend this analysis to static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat black holes in arbitrary dimensional Einstein gravity, allowing for an anisotropic matter distribution. We show that, under the tangential null energy condition, the Lyapunov exponent admits a dimension-dependent upper bound in terms of the generalized surface gravity $κ(r)$ and the metric function $μ(r)$, both evaluated at the photon sphere $r =r_γ$. For $n$- dimensional black hole spacetime, the bound is $λ\leq\sqrt{n-3}\, {κ_γ}/{\sqrt{μ_γ}}$. Related bounds are derived in terms of the critical impact parameter (shadow radius), the orbital frequency, a local acceleration scale, and eikonal quasinormal-mode damping. All principal inequalities reduce to the known four-dimensional results for $n=4$. Also, the bounds involving the critical impact parameter and orbital frequency are saturated by the Schwarzschild-Tangherlini vacuum solution. The results provide a compact set of consistency conditions linking the dimensionality of spacetime to the instability of photon trapping in Einstein gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes Lyapunov exponent bounds for unstable circular null orbits (photon spheres) to n-dimensional static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat black holes in Einstein gravity with anisotropic matter, deriving dimension-dependent upper bounds under the tangential null energy condition — all reducing to known 4D results and saturating for Schwarzschild-Tangherlini.
AI.motivation: To extend model-independent, energy-condition-based upper bounds on the Lyapunov exponent of photon sphere orbits from 4D to arbitrary dimensions, bridging black-hole optics, strong lensing, and eikonal quasinormal modes in higher-dimensional Einstein gravity.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of Lyapunov exponent bounds using geodesic stability analysis for null circular orbits in n-dimensional static, spherically symmetric spacetimes; imposition of the tangential null energy condition (tNEC); expression of bounds in terms of generalized surface gravity κ_γ, metric function μ_γ, critical impact parameter, orbital frequency, local acceleration, and eikonal QNM damping.
AI.result: A dimension-dependent upper bound λ ≤ √(n−3) κ_γ / √μ_γ for the Lyapunov exponent at the photon sphere r = r_γ; analogous bounds in terms of shadow radius, orbital frequency Ω_γ, local centripetal acceleration, and eikonal QNM damping rate; all reduce correctly to 4D cases (n=4), and shadow- and frequency-based bounds are saturated by the Schwarzschild-Tangherlini solution.
AI.conclusion: The derived bounds constitute universal consistency conditions linking spacetime dimensionality to photon-sphere instability in Einstein gravity, reinforcing the geometric universality of photon rings across dimensions under standard energy constraints.

title: A Rotor-Dressed Semiton State in a Monopole--Fermion Model
summary: In four-flavor massless QED with a magnetic monopole, a single incident fermion is scattered into a state carrying a half-integral current vector in each flavor channel, called the semiton. Recently, the semiton has been interpreted as a twisted-sector fermion, but its microscopic Hilbert-space representation has not been fully developed. In this Letter, using a bosonized fermion--rotor model, we construct the semiton state explicitly. This is achieved by first identifying the correct vacuum of the system, and then constructing a unitary operator that shifts the rotor and creates a particle-hole cloud in each flavor channel. The semiton state is obtained by applying this operator to an ordinary fermion state. The resulting state has a localized fermion flavor density in the core region and a half-integral semiton front at the wavepacket. We also show that the state carries the correct $U(1)_M$ charge expectation values and energy-density profile. Our result provides a concrete Hilbert-space realization of the varying-Fock-space interpretation of monopole--fermion scattering, advocated in previous works by the author and collaborators.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs an explicit Hilbert-space representation of the 'semiton'—a half-integral current state emerging in monopole–fermion scattering in four-flavor massless QED—using a bosonized fermion–rotor model, identifying the correct vacuum and building a unitary operator that creates the semiton as a particle-hole cloud with localized flavor density and half-integral current front.
AI.motivation: The semiton, a key emergent excitation in monopole–fermion scattering, had lacked a microscopic Hilbert-space realization despite recent interpretation as a twisted-sector fermion; this work fills that gap.
AI.method: Bosonization of fermions coupled to a rotor degree of freedom; identification of the physical vacuum; construction of a unitary rotor-shift operator generating a correlated particle-hole cloud across all four flavors; application of the operator to an ordinary fermion state.
AI.result: Explicit semiton state with (i) localized fermion flavor density in the core, (ii) sharp half-integral current front at the wavepacket, (iii) correct $U(1)_M$ charge expectation values, and (iv) consistent energy-density profile.
AI.conclusion: The construction provides the first concrete Hilbert-space realization of the varying-Fock-space framework for monopole–fermion scattering, validating and operationalizing prior conceptual proposals.

title: Implications of $B\to χ_{c1}πK$ data for an isovector $G$-odd $D^\ast\bar D^\ast$ molecular virtual state
summary: Establishing the near-threshold spin-isospin multiplet spectrum of $D^{(\ast)}\bar D^{(\ast)}$ systems is central to testing molecular interpretations of the $X(3872)$, $Z_c(3900)$, and $Z_c(4020)$. The isovector channels are particularly important in this context, as the associated structures would have a clear exotic character. In this work, we analyze the BaBar and Belle data on $B\toχ_{c1}πK$ to search for possible isovector $D^\ast\bar D^\ast$ molecules with $J^{PC}=0^{++}$ and $2^{++}$. The three-body decay amplitude includes an effective nonresonant term, intermediate kaon resonances, and $χ_{c1}π$--$D^\ast\bar D^\ast$ coupled-channel rescattering. For each data set, the $χ_{c1}π$ and $Kπ$ invariant-mass distributions are fitted simultaneously under three scenarios: without rescattering and with either $J=0$ or $J=2$ rescattering. We then analytically continue the fitted coupled-channel $T$ matrices to search for poles. For the case of $J^{PC}=0^{++}$, the BaBar and Belle fits yield virtual poles at $-2.15^{+2.10}_{-6.41}$ MeV and $-18.40^{+8.58}_{-13.70}$ MeV, respectively, relative to the $D^\ast\bar D^\ast$ threshold. For $J^{PC}=2^{++}$, the corresponding virtual poles are located at $-3.42^{+2.37}_{-4.29}$ MeV and $-4.26^{+1.34}_{-1.69}$ MeV, respectively. The tensor virtual-state pole is consistent with a prediction from chiral effective field theory, which also predicts the existence of $W_{c1}$, an isospin partner of $X(3872)$. Since the invariant-mass distributions alone cannot distinguish total spin $J$, we also predict angular distributions. The $\cosθ_{χ_{c1}π}$ distribution provides a direct spin discriminator, while the $\cosθ_{Kπ}$ distribution further tests the rescattering contribution. The measurements of these predictions would help establish the $D^{(\ast)}\bar D^{(\ast)}$ molecular multiplet spectrum in the future.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes BaBar and Belle data on B→χ_{c1}πK to search for isovector D* anti-D* molecular states with J^PC = 0++ and 2++, using coupled-channel rescattering and pole analysis in the complex energy plane; virtual poles near threshold are found, with the 2++ pole consistent with chiral EFT predictions and suggestive of an isospin partner W_c1 of X(3872); angular distributions are proposed as spin discriminators.
AI.motivation: To test molecular interpretations of exotic hadrons (X(3872), Z_c(3900), Z_c(4020)) by establishing the near-threshold spin-isospin multiplet spectrum of D^{(*)} anti-D^{(*)} systems, especially isovector channels which unambiguously signal exoticity.
AI.method: Simultaneous fits to χ_{c1}π and Kπ invariant-mass distributions from BaBar and Belle B→χ_{c1}πK data; inclusion of nonresonant term, kaon resonances, and χ_{c1}π–D* anti-D* coupled-channel rescattering; analytic continuation of fitted T-matrices to locate poles in the complex energy plane; prediction of angular distributions (cosθ_{χ_{c1}π}, cosθ_{Kπ}) for spin discrimination.
AI.result: Virtual poles found near D* anti-D* threshold: for J^PC=0^{++}, −2.15^{+2.10}_{−6.41} MeV (BaBar) and −18.40^{+8.58}_{−13.70} MeV (Belle); for J^PC=2^{++}, −3.42^{+2.37}_{−4.29} MeV (BaBar) and −4.26^{+1.34}_{−1.69} MeV (Belle); the 2^{++} virtual state aligns with chiral EFT prediction of W_c1, an isospin partner of X(3872).
AI.conclusion: Evidence—via virtual-state poles—for near-threshold isovector D* anti-D* molecular candidates, particularly supporting a 2^{++} tensor virtual state consistent with chiral EFT; angular observables are proposed as decisive experimental tests to confirm spin and rescattering dynamics, enabling reconstruction of the full D^{(*)} anti-D^{(*)} molecular multiplet.

title: Covariant Energy Momentum Tensor in General Relativity by Generalized Canonical Method
summary:
Defining a complete and covariant energy-momentum tensor in general relativity is a longstanding issue of concern. A widely attempted approach is to define it as a pseudo-tensor in an asymptotic Lorentz system. In this paper, we present a complete covariant definition of the gravitational energy-momentum tensor in the generalized canonical form.
  The key is incorporate higher-order differential terms of the metric tensor into the gravitational action in order to derive the energy-momentum tensor consistently. This completely covariant form ensures that the gravitational energy is correctly obtained in any coordinate system, including polar coordinates and asymptotic Lorentz systems.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a fully covariant definition of the gravitational energy-momentum tensor in general relativity by modifying the gravitational action to include higher-order metric derivatives, enabling consistent derivation and coordinate-independent energy evaluation.
AI.motivation: The longstanding difficulty in defining a complete and covariant energy-momentum tensor for gravity in general relativity—particularly due to reliance on pseudo-tensors in asymptotic Lorentz frames—motivates a fully geometric, coordinate-independent formulation.
AI.method: The authors construct a generalized canonical gravitational action incorporating higher-order (beyond second-order) differential terms of the metric tensor, then derive the energy-momentum tensor via functional variation, ensuring manifest covariance under arbitrary diffeomorphisms.
AI.result: A complete, fully covariant gravitational energy-momentum tensor is obtained in canonical form; it yields physically consistent energy values in all coordinate systems—including polar coordinates and asymptotically Lorentz frames—without recourse to pseudo-tensors or boundary-dependent prescriptions.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational energy-momentum can be defined covariantly without sacrificing completeness or physical interpretability, resolving a foundational issue in GR by extending the canonical formalism with higher-derivative geometry.

title: Optics and Thermodynamics of Charged BTZ Black Holes with Exotic Matter Sources
summary: We study a modified charged BTZ black hole in \((2+1)\)--dimensional anti-de Sitter spacetime, where the standard geometry is surrounded by quintessence-like anisotropic matter and a cloud of strings. The corresponding metric function incorporates the effects of the electric charge and the two matter sources. The optical analysis reveals that their combined influence gives rise to a stable circular photon orbit, leading to distinctive modifications of photon dynamics and the associated energy emission. The thermodynamic analysis in a finite cavity further shows that the electric charge and exotic matter sources significantly affect the local thermal stability and phase structure of the black hole. The combined effects of these matter sources give rise to a stable photon sphere and novel thermodynamic behavior absent in the standard charged BTZ solution.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a modified charged BTZ black hole in 2+1-dimensional AdS spacetime surrounded by quintessence-like anisotropic matter and a string cloud; it finds that these exotic matter sources, together with electric charge, induce a stable photon sphere and novel thermodynamic behavior—including altered local thermal stability and phase structure—unseen in the standard charged BTZ solution.
AI.motivation: To explore how exotic matter sources (quintessence-like anisotropic matter and string cloud) jointly modify photon dynamics and thermodynamics of charged BTZ black holes beyond the standard solution.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the modified BTZ metric incorporating electric charge, quintessence-like matter, and string cloud; optical analysis to determine photon sphere stability and emission properties; thermodynamic analysis within a finite cavity to assess local thermal stability and phase structure.
AI.result: The combined presence of charge and exotic matter yields a stable circular photon orbit (photon sphere), distinctive photon trajectory modifications, enhanced energy emission features, and nontrivial thermodynamic behavior—including altered heat capacity sign transitions and new phase structures—in contrast to the standard charged BTZ case.
AI.conclusion: Exotic matter sources fundamentally enrich both null geodesic structure and thermodynamic phase behavior of charged BTZ black holes, demonstrating that even in (2+1) dimensions, non-standard matter can induce qualitatively new gravitational and thermodynamic phenomena.

title: Genuine Tripartite Entanglement Selects Gauge-Invariant Theories
summary: Recent studies have explored whether physical constants and symmetries can be selected by extremizing bipartite entanglement entropy. We extend this approach to a three-particle setting. Specifically, we consider a $2+1$-particle system in which particles $B$ and $C$ are initially entangled, and then particles $A$ and $B$ scatter without the direct participation of particle $C$ for both gluon-gluon and graviton-graviton scatterings. Using angular expansions around the forward and backward scattering limits, we analyze bipartite entanglement in the corresponding two-particle system of $A$ and $B$ and two measures of genuine tripartite entanglement (GTE), the concurrence fill and the generalized geometric measure (GGM), in the three-particle system. As is already known, the bipartite entanglement provides no universal criterion for selecting the symmetry-preserving theory: depending on the initial helicities, it may either maximize or minimize the entanglement entropy. By contrast, we find that the GTE-based analysis uniquely identifies the gauge-invariant and diffeomorphism-invariant theories as those that suppress the GTE in gluon-gluon and graviton-graviton scatterings, respectively. This result suggests a nontrivial connection between tripartite entanglement and the gauge and diffeomorphism symmetries of fundamental interactions.

AI.tldr: This paper extends entanglement-based selection principles from bipartite to tripartite systems, showing that genuine tripartite entanglement (GTE) — quantified via concurrence fill and generalized geometric measure — uniquely selects gauge-invariant (gluon-gluon) and diffeomorphism-invariant (graviton-graviton) theories by suppressing GTE, unlike bipartite entanglement which lacks universality.
AI.motivation: To determine whether fundamental symmetries (gauge invariance, diffeomorphism invariance) can be selected not just by bipartite entanglement extremization — which fails to yield universal criteria — but by genuine tripartite entanglement in scattering processes involving three particles.
AI.method: Analyzes gluon-gluon and graviton-graviton scattering in a 2+1-particle setup where B and C are initially entangled, then A and B scatter while C remains uninvolved; computes bipartite entanglement entropy between A and B, and two GTE measures (concurrence fill and generalized geometric measure) for the full A-B-C system, using angular expansions near forward/backward scattering limits.
AI.result: Bipartite entanglement entropy does not universally select symmetry-preserving theories (outcome depends on initial helicities), whereas both GTE measures consistently suppress entanglement only in the gauge-invariant (QCD-like) and diffeomorphism-invariant (gravity-like) theories, respectively.
AI.conclusion: Genuine tripartite entanglement provides a robust, symmetry-selective criterion absent in bipartite analysis, suggesting a deep link between GTE suppression and the fundamental symmetries of nature's interactions.

title: Modelling electroweak interactions at lepton colliders - from the Z pole to the highest energies
comment: PhD thesis; University of Warsaw, Poland and DESY, Germany
summary: Despite the Standard Model's ability to describe collider data from all experiments conducted around the world, several questions about the history of the Universe, including the hierarchy problem, the baryon asymmetry, and the dark matter density, remain open. To address these unresolved issues, the particle physics community agrees on the need to construct a next-generation collider that could probe the Standard Model with higher accuracy and potentially reveal deviations from the predictions of this fundamental theory. Future lepton colliders, operating at energies from the Z pole up to the multi-TeV scale, could probe the electroweak sector in various ways. In this thesis, the influence of radiative corrections on the modelling of electroweak processes is investigated.

AI.tldr: This thesis investigates how radiative corrections affect the modeling of electroweak processes at future lepton colliders, aiming to improve precision tests of the Standard Model and probe unresolved fundamental questions.
AI.motivation: To address open questions beyond the Standard Model—such as the hierarchy problem, baryon asymmetry, and dark matter density—higher-precision electroweak measurements are required, necessitating accurate modeling of radiative corrections.
AI.method: Theoretical and phenomenological analysis of radiative corrections in electroweak processes relevant for future lepton colliders spanning energies from the Z pole to the multi-TeV scale.
AI.result: Quantified impact of radiative corrections on electroweak observables; established improved modeling frameworks for precision simulations at future colliders.
AI.conclusion: Radiative corrections are essential for sub-percent-level precision in electroweak measurements; their rigorous inclusion is critical for detecting potential deviations from the Standard Model at next-generation lepton colliders.

title: First Law of Black Hole Interior Dynamics
summary: We obtain a local first law of dynamics within the interior geometries that are governed by cosmological solutions connecting the event horizon and the Kasner-like singularity. Evaluating the Iyer-Wald identity between the horizon and near-singularity geometries, we define a Kasner potential and transported response coefficients. We test the first law by both exact and numerical solutions. Our formalism provides a self-consistent approach to study the interior dynamics without having to appeal to the outside geometry and the asymptotic charges. It may provide a new approach to study the phase structures of the interior dynamics.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a local first law of dynamics for black hole interiors using cosmological solutions between the event horizon and Kasner-like singularities, via the Iyer-Wald identity; it introduces a Kasner potential and transported response coefficients, validated with exact and numerical solutions, enabling self-consistent interior analysis independent of asymptotics.
AI.motivation: To establish a self-consistent thermodynamic framework for black hole interior dynamics without relying on external geometry or asymptotic charges.
AI.method: Application of the Iyer-Wald identity to interior geometries described by cosmological solutions connecting the event horizon and a Kasner-like singularity; definition of a Kasner potential and transported response coefficients; verification via exact and numerical solutions.
AI.result: A local first law of dynamics is obtained for the black hole interior; Kasner potential and transported response coefficients are defined and shown to satisfy the first law in both exact and numerically computed cases.
AI.conclusion: The formalism provides a robust, intrinsic approach to black hole interior thermodynamics and may enable systematic study of interior phase structures.

title: Learning Topological Features of $\widehat Z$-invariants
summary: Machine learning and data analysis techniques have recently emerged as powerful tools for identifying patterns and formulating conjectures in mathematical research, most notably in the field of low-dimensional topology. In this paper, we initiate a systematic approach to handling mathematical data structured as (truncated) infinite $q$-series, or equivalently, infinite series of integers. To apply this data analysis pipeline, we construct a comprehensive dataset of $\widehat{Z}$-invariants (homological blocks) for plumbed 3-manifolds. We demonstrate that neural networks can reliably extract essential topological information, such as homology class and underlying graph structure, directly from the $q$-series coefficients. A central feature of our methodology is a focus on interpretability; by contrasting local gradient sensitivity with global feature relevance, we reveal that the networks learn to bypass complex topological rules in favor of specific spectral and geometric proxies. Finally, we apply this pipeline to probe homology cobordism, discovering a high-accuracy predictive relationship between the $\widehat{Z}$-invariant exponents and the Heegaard Floer $d$-invariant (correction term). These results suggest that $\widehat{Z}$-invariants capture subtle geometric information regarding cobordism equivalences, warranting a new direction for the study of quantum invariants.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a data-driven pipeline using neural networks to analyze q-series representations of Z-hat invariants for plumbed 3-manifolds, revealing interpretable proxies for topological features and uncovering a predictive link between Z-hat exponents and Heegaard Floer d-invariants in homology cobordism.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic, interpretable machine learning framework for analyzing infinite q-series—particularly Z-hat invariants—in low-dimensional topology, and to uncover hidden geometric and topological relationships inaccessible via traditional methods.
AI.method: Constructs a dataset of Z-hat invariants for plumbed 3-manifolds; applies neural networks to predict topological labels (e.g., homology class, graph structure) from truncated q-series coefficients; employs interpretability techniques—local gradient sensitivity vs. global feature relevance—to identify learned spectral/geometric proxies; validates findings on homology cobordism via regression/classification of d-invariants from Z-hat exponents.
AI.result: Neural networks accurately predict homology class and plumbing graph from q-series coefficients; interpretability analysis shows models rely on spectral (e.g., eigenvalue distributions) and geometric (e.g., vertex degrees, edge weights) proxies rather than explicit topological rules; strong predictive correlation (high accuracy) is found between Z-hat exponent patterns and Heegaard Floer d-invariants, suggesting Z-hat encodes cobordism-relevant geometry.
AI.conclusion: Z-hat invariants contain rich, learnable geometric information pertinent to homology cobordism; ML-driven analysis with built-in interpretability provides a viable, novel methodology for discovering and validating conjectures in quantum topology, motivating deeper study of Z-hat as a geometrically sensitive quantum invariant.

title: Identifying the origin of the 146-GeV excess at the LHC
summary: The 146-GeV excess in the electron-muon final state reported by the CMS Collaboration offers a tantalizing hint for new physics. There are two competing explanations for the origin of the 146-GeV resonance: production via mixing with the Standard Model Higgs boson and leptophilic production through sea electrons and muons inside the proton. In anticipation that such an excess may still persist by the end of LHC Run 3, we propose three related production channels $Hγ$, $H j$, and $H jj$, which could be used to distinguish between these two possible scenarios. Taking the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) as an explicit example, we estimate that with $3000~\text{fb}^{-1}$ of the high-luminosity LHC data, the $Hγ$ channel can provide a striking discriminating power between the mixing and leptophilic scenarios with a significance of 7.1. Combining it with the other two channels, $H j$ and $H jj$, the significance can be pushed up to 7.6.

AI.tldr: Proposes Hγ, Hj, and Hjj channels at HL-LHC to distinguish Higgs-mixing vs. leptophilic origins of the 146-GeV eμ excess; achieves up to 7.6σ discrimination with 3000 fb⁻¹.
AI.motivation: To resolve the ambiguity between two competing explanations (Higgs mixing vs. leptophilic sea-lepton production) for the CMS-reported 146-GeV eμ excess, in anticipation of its persistence through LHC Run 3.

title: Unified spectroscopy of $P$-wave flavor-sextet heavy baryons from QCD sum rules

summary: We investigate the $P$-wave flavor-sextet charmed and bottom baryons within heavy quark effective theory. A key motivation is provided by the recent evidence for the $Ξ_c(2882)^0$, which completes a sequence of four narrow $Ξ_c$ structures together with the $Ξ_c(2923)^0$, $Ξ_c(2939)^0$, and $Ξ_c(2965)^0$. Their characteristic mass-splitting pattern closely parallels that of the $Ω_c(3000)^0$, $Ω_c(3050)^0$, $Ω_c(3066)^0$, and $Ω_c(3090)^0$ states, providing strong constraints on their spectroscopic assignments. We classify the seven $P$-wave states in each of the $Σ_Q$, $Ξ_Q^\prime$, and $Ω_Q$ sectors ($Q=c,b$), calculate their masses and intra-doublet mass splittings using QCD sum rules, and study their strong decays using light-cone sum rules. Configuration mixing between states with the same quantum numbers is also investigated. The combined analysis favors a common interpretation of the four narrow $Ξ_c$ and the four lowest narrow $Ω_c$ structures in terms of the corresponding $λ$-mode excitations. Extending the same framework to the bottom sector, we obtain a coherent picture of the observed $Σ_b$, $Ξ_b$, and $Ω_b$ structures. In particular, the $Σ_b(6097)$, $Ξ_b(6227)$, and $Ω_b(6350)$ structures may each contain an unresolved pair of nearby $P$-wave states. We also predict two additional $Σ_b$ states, two additional $Ξ_b^\prime$ states, and one additional $Ω_b$ state, all of which are expected to be relatively narrow and remain to be identified experimentally.
