title: Entanglement islands and information recovery from near-extremal regular black holes
summary: We investigate the Page curve and information recovery in a near-extremal regular black hole inspired by T-duality, in which the central singularity is resolved by a minimal length scale. By integrating the first law of thermodynamics at fixed minimal length, we obtain a black-hole entropy containing an intrinsically quantum logarithmic correction, while the area-law contribution vanishes in the extremal limit. Consequently, the extremal remnant carries a finite entropy of purely quantum origin. Using the island prescription in the near-horizon regime, we evaluate the generalized entropy of radiation and compare the standard area functional with an alternative functional constructed from the corrected thermodynamic entropy of the black hole. In the near-extremal limit, the latter reduces analytically to the classical extremization problem with an effective coupling, and it places the physical island closer to the outer horizon. Although both prescriptions produce a Page transition, they predict different saturation values and Page times. While the standard functional yields a plateau controlled by the area term, the corrected prescription saturates at the full thermodynamic entropy of the outer horizon and, in the extremal limit, at the logarithmic remnant entropy. Including evaporation and backreaction, the Page curve develops the expected descending branch and asymptotes to the entropy of the cold extremal remnant rather than to zero. Our results indicate that a thermodynamically consistent description of information recovery from regular near-extremal black holes requires incorporating the intrinsic quantum correction to the gravitational entropy.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the Page curve and information recovery in a near-extremal regular black hole model inspired by T-duality, where the singularity is resolved by a minimal length. It derives a quantum-corrected black hole entropy with a vanishing area-law term in the extremal limit—leaving only a finite logarithmic (quantum) remnant entropy. Using the island prescription, it compares two generalized entropy functionals: one standard (area-based), one thermodynamically corrected. The latter yields a physically closer island, distinct Page time and saturation value (matching full thermodynamic entropy, including the extremal remnant’s logarithmic entropy), and an asymptotic Page curve descending to the remnant’s entropy—not zero—when evaporation and backreaction are included.
AI.motivation: To reconcile unitary information recovery (via the Page curve and island paradigm) with thermodynamically consistent entropy for regular black holes that resolve singularities via quantum geometry (e.g., T-duality-induced minimal length), especially in the physically relevant near-extremal regime where conventional area-law entropy fails.
AI.method: 1) Derive black hole entropy from first law of thermodynamics at fixed minimal length, yielding area-law suppression and intrinsic logarithmic quantum correction; 2) Apply the island prescription in the near-horizon region to compute generalized entropy of radiation; 3) Compare two entropy functionals: (a) standard Bekenstein–Hawking area functional, (b) alternative functional built from the derived thermodynamically consistent (logarithmically corrected) entropy; 4) Analyze Page transition, saturation, island location, and asymptotic behavior under Hawking evaporation and backreaction.
AI.result: Both entropy prescriptions yield a Page transition, but the corrected functional predicts: (i) island located closer to the outer horizon; (ii) earlier Page time; (iii) saturation at the full thermodynamic entropy of the outer horizon (not just its area); (iv) in the extremal limit, saturation at the finite logarithmic remnant entropy; (v) asymptotic Page curve descending to the cold remnant’s entropy—not zero—when evaporation and backreaction are included.
AI.conclusion: A thermodynamically consistent description of information recovery in regular near-extremal black holes necessitates incorporating intrinsic quantum corrections (e.g., logarithmic entropy) into the gravitational entropy used in the island rule—standard area-law prescriptions are insufficient, particularly for extremal remnants.

title: $Υ(nS)$ Production within Jets at the LHC
summary: Heavy quarkonium production inside jets offers a sensitive probe of QCD dynamics and bound-state formation mechanisms. While recent studies demonstrate that charmonium-in-jet observables effectively discriminate among competing nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) long-distance matrix element (LDME) sets, whether this discriminating power persists in the bottomonium sector remains an open question. Here, we present the first phenomenological study of $Υ(1S)$, $Υ(2S)$, and $Υ(3S)$ production inside jets using the fragmenting jet function (FJF) framework at next-to-leading order (NLO), incorporating DGLAP evolution, threshold resummation, and feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states. In sharp contrast to charmonium, we find that bottomonium-in-jet momentum-fraction ($z_H$) distributions exhibit a universal shape that is remarkably insensitive to the choice of LDME sets. We show that this universality stems from the strong dominance of the S-wave spin-triplet color-octet ($^3S_1^{[8]}$) production mechanism reinforced by $χ_b$ feeddown transitions. Our predictions capture both the characteristic large-$z_H$ peak and the spectral broadening with increasing jet transverse momentum observed in recent CMS measurements. These results establish a clear physical distinction between charmonium and bottomonium fragmentation inside jets, providing a theoretical benchmark for future high-precision measurements at the LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first NLO phenomenological study of bottomonium (Υ(1S), Υ(2S), Υ(3S)) production inside jets using the fragmenting jet function framework, finding universal z_H distributions insensitive to LDME choices—unlike charmonium—due to dominant ^3S_1^[8] production and χ_b feeddown; predictions match CMS data on large-z_H peak and spectral broadening.
AI.motivation: To determine whether bottomonium-in-jet observables retain the LDME-discriminating power previously observed for charmonium, given open questions about universality and formation mechanisms in the heavier bottomonium sector.
AI.method: Next-to-leading order (NLO) calculation within the fragmenting jet function (FJF) framework, including DGLAP evolution, threshold resummation, and feeddown from higher bottomonium states (e.g., χ_b → Υ); applied to Υ(1S), Υ(2S), and Υ(3S) production inside jets.
AI.result: Bottomonium-in-jet z_H distributions are universal across LDME sets—unlike charmonium—driven by dominance of the color-octet ^3S_1^[8] channel and χ_b feeddown; predictions reproduce CMS observations: a pronounced large-z_H peak and jet-pT-dependent spectral broadening.
AI.conclusion: Bottomonium fragmentation inside jets is fundamentally distinct from charmonium due to mechanistic universality, establishing a robust theoretical benchmark for LHC precision tests and constraining NRQCD interpretations of quarkonium formation.

title: Effective curvature coupling of link-based causal set propagators in $1+1$ dimensions
summary: We study how a recently introduced causal-set propagator defined in terms of links responds to curvature. On sprinklings embedded in a flat 1+1-dimensional Minkowski space, this propagator is known to reproduce the massless retarded continuum Greens function on large scales. In conformally flat embeddings with constant curvature $\mathcal R$, the causal order is unchanged, but the link relationship is sensitive to the physical volume of the spanned causal diamond. We show that this volume dependence generates a leading curvature correction to the propagator. On large distances, this correction is equivalent to a continuum scalar propagator with an effective curvature coupling of the form $ξ\mathcal R$ with the coupling constant $ξ_{\rm eff}=1/6$, equivalently corresponding to an effective mass-squared parameter $m_{\rm eff}^2=ξ_{\rm eff}\mathcal R$. This coupling is not inserted by hand but emerges from the link-based path sum itself, reflecting the microscopic structure of the causal set. Numerical simulations on sprinklings embedded in $\mathrm{AdS}_{1+1}$ and $\mathrm{dS}_{1+1}$ support the predicted curvature response and indicate that the effective coupling persists as the sprinkling density is increased.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how a causal-set propagator, defined via links, responds to spacetime curvature in 1+1 dimensions; it finds that curvature corrections emerge naturally from the link-based path sum, yielding an effective curvature coupling ξ_eff = 1/6 — matching the conformal coupling — confirmed numerically in AdS and dS backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To understand how discrete causal-set quantum gravity models encode and respond to spacetime curvature, specifically whether continuum geometric features like curvature coupling can emerge from purely combinatorial (link-based) structures without ad hoc insertion.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the curvature correction to the link-based causal-set propagator in conformally flat 1+1D spacetimes with constant scalar curvature ℛ; comparison with continuum retarded Green’s functions; numerical simulations on Poisson sprinklings into AdS₁₊₁ and dS₁₊₁ to test scaling and density dependence.
AI.result: The link-based propagator acquires a leading-order curvature correction equivalent to a continuum scalar field with ξ_eff = 1/6 (i.e., m²_eff = ℛ/6); this emerges intrinsically from the volume dependence of causal diamonds spanned by links; numerical results confirm the predicted correction and its persistence under increased sprinkling density.
AI.conclusion: Curvature coupling — specifically the conformal value ξ = 1/6 — is not imposed but dynamically emergent from the causal-set’s microscopic link structure, supporting the viability of causal sets as a background-independent quantum gravity framework where geometry and field dynamics co-arise.

title: Spin precession and anomalous dipole couplings in a plane-wave Yang-Mills background
summary: We investigate the fermion spin dynamics and induced dipole interactions in an external Yang-Mills gauge field that represents a non-Abelian plane wave. We use the exact solutions of the Dirac equation in the external gauge field, the exact fermion Green's function, and the renormalized one-loop fermion-gluon vertex in the axial gauge. The exact propagator produces spin-dependent structures proportional to $σ^{μν}F_{μν}^{a} $. The external field induces spin precession at tree level through a non-Abelian extension of the Bargmann-Michel-Telegdi equation, coupled with Wong color transport. The exact vertex produces a phase-dependent Pauli form factor $F_{2}^{a}\left( 0;\varphi ,\varphi ^{\prime }\right) $ beyond tree level, which serves as an anomalous chromomagnetic dipole coupling. For monochromatic two-color noncommuting plane waves, explicit weak-field expressions are derived for the induced Pauli coefficient and the anomalous spin-precession frequency. The commutator term $gf^{abc}A_{μ}^{b}A_{ν}^{c}$ in this case, generates additional field-strength components and dynamically induced precession axes not present in Abelian backgrounds, resulting in coupled spin-color precession. The exact one-loop coefficient is provided as a harmonic expansion suitable for periodic Yang-Mills waves. Explicit expressions for spin-dependent amplitudes, spin-flip probabilities, and polarization asymmetries are provided. These results establish a direct connection between exact background-field propagators, renormalized vertex functions, anomalous dipole interactions, and observable spin effects in strong non-Abelian gauge fields.

AI.tldr: This paper studies fermion spin dynamics and induced dipole interactions in a non-Abelian (Yang-Mills) plane-wave gauge field, deriving exact and weak-field results for spin precession, anomalous chromomagnetic dipole coupling, and observable spin effects such as spin-flip probabilities and polarization asymmetries.
AI.motivation: To understand how strong non-Abelian gauge fields—beyond the Abelian (QED-like) limit—affect fermion spin dynamics, particularly through induced dipole interactions, anomalous couplings, and coupled spin-color precession not present in electromagnetic backgrounds.
AI.method: Uses exact solutions of the Dirac equation and exact fermion Green's function in a non-Abelian plane-wave background; employs renormalized one-loop fermion-gluon vertex in axial gauge; derives weak-field expansions for monochromatic two-color noncommuting plane waves; analyzes spin-dependent structures, Pauli form factors, and precession frequencies via Wong equations and non-Abelian BMT generalization.
AI.result: Derives tree-level non-Abelian Bargmann-Michel-Telegdi–Wong spin-color precession; obtains a phase-dependent one-loop Pauli form factor $F_2^a(0;\varphi,\varphi')$ representing anomalous chromomagnetic dipole coupling; identifies commutator-induced field-strength components and novel precession axes; provides harmonic expansion of the one-loop coefficient for periodic waves; gives explicit expressions for spin-flip probabilities and polarization asymmetries.
AI.conclusion: Exact background-field techniques and renormalized vertex functions directly link non-Abelian field structure to observable spin effects—establishing a framework for probing strong-field QCD-like dynamics via spin-polarized probes.

title: Revisiting Quark-Lepton Complementarity in the Precision Neutrino Era
summary: We revisit three-generation quark-lepton complementarity in the non-trivial correlation-matrix formulation using the 2026 Particle Data Group quark-mixing inputs and the NuFIT 6.1 oscillation likelihood release. First, we perform a retrospective test of the narrow atmospheric-angle prediction published in 2016. Its central value receives likelihood penalties of 17.99 and 20.43 for normal and inverted ordering, respectively, whereas later ordering-dependent predictions lie close to the current likelihood minima. We then reconstruct a projection-weighted ensemble of the full complex correlation matrix, retaining unrestricted quark-lepton mismatch phases and exact sample-wise unitarity. The first row remains comparatively stable, while the lower two rows account for about 99% of the decade-long mean-texture evolution. The strongest normal-inverted differences occur in the third-row elements, with distribution-overlap coefficients of about 0.41 and 0.42 for the first two entries. Approximately 72% of the present ensemble remains closer to a tribimaximal than to a bimaximal reference texture. The results show that the broad quark-lepton correlation structure is substantially more persistent than the most restrictive atmospheric-angle prediction derived from it.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines three-generation quark-lepton complementarity using updated experimental data (PDG 2026, NuFIT 6.1), finds the 2016 narrow atmospheric-angle prediction strongly disfavored (Δχ² ≈ 18–20), reconstructs a unitary, phase-resolved complex correlation matrix, reveals strong ordering-dependent differences in the third row, and shows ~72% of the ensemble prefers tribimaximal over bimaximal texture — indicating robustness of the broader correlation structure despite failure of specific predictions.
AI.motivation: To test the empirical validity and stability of quark-lepton complementarity—particularly the 2016 atmospheric-angle prediction—and to assess how the full complex correlation matrix evolves with improved data and whether its structure persists across neutrino mass orderings.
AI.method: Uses PDG 2026 quark-mixing parameters and NuFIT 6.1 neutrino oscillation likelihoods; performs likelihood-based retrospective validation; constructs a projection-weighted ensemble of the full 3×3 complex correlation matrix with unrestricted mismatch phases and exact unitarity; quantifies stability via row-wise evolution, distribution overlap coefficients, and texture proximity (tribimaximal vs. bimaximal).
AI.result: The 2016 atmospheric-angle prediction is penalized by Δχ² = 17.99 (NO) and 20.43 (IO); later ordering-dependent predictions align near current best-fit points; first row of correlation matrix is stable; lower two rows drive ~99% of decade-long texture evolution; third-row elements show strongest NO–IO differentiation (overlap ~0.41–0.42); ~72% of ensemble favors tribimaximal texture.
AI.conclusion: The broad quark-lepton correlation structure is highly persistent and resilient to data updates, whereas highly restrictive phenomenological predictions (e.g., narrow atmospheric-angle relation) are empirically excluded—highlighting the need for flexible, unitary, phase-aware formulations of complementarity.

title: A Quantum-Gravity-Motivated GUP Effective Metric
summary: Recent critiques have addressed certain aspects of the generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) effective metric (Ong 2023). This study presents a scale-dependent quadratic GUP effective metric, constructed through analyses of the gravity-induced phase shift (COW experiment) and the Einstein-Bohr photon box Gedanken experiment. In contrast to the procedure outlined in (Xiang et al. 2018), the momentum-dependent metric is improved by introducing an interpolating function $Δp (r)$, which employs the effective distance concept to accurately capture the distinct behavior of $Δp (r)$ in both short and long distance regimes. The resulting effective metric exhibits the same structure as that derived from the Renormalization Group (RG) theory. However, the RG parameter $\hatγ$ can now be related to the dimensionless GUP parameter $β_0$, thereby distinguishing this metric from the RG-based approach. The corresponding effective metric prediction demonstrates internal consistency of the model, and phenomenologically the predictions are in agreement with some quantum black hole models in some limits. The effective metric improved black hole thermodynamics and shadow predictions compared to the heuristic approach and other proposed GUP effective metrics. Furthermore, the relationship between GUP and $f(R)$ gravity (D'Agostino et al. 2026) may provide a possible future route toward a more fundamental description of GUP.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a scale-dependent quadratic GUP effective metric using COW and Einstein-Bohr photon box experiments, improves momentum dependence via an interpolating function Δp(r), links the RG parameter γ̂ to the GUP parameter β₀, and shows enhanced consistency and phenomenological agreement—especially in black hole thermodynamics and shadow predictions—compared to prior heuristic or RG-based GUP metrics.
AI.motivation: To address limitations in existing GUP effective metrics—particularly their lack of scale dependence and inconsistent momentum behavior across distance regimes—and to establish a physically grounded, internally consistent bridge between GUP and effective spacetime geometry.
AI.method: Constructs a quadratic GUP effective metric by analyzing gravity-induced phase shifts (COW experiment) and the Einstein-Bohr photon box Gedankenexperiment; introduces an interpolating momentum uncertainty function Δp(r) based on effective distance to capture short- and long-distance behavior; derives metric structure matching RG flow but with γ̂ explicitly tied to β₀; validates internal consistency and compares predictions with quantum black hole models and f(R) gravity correspondence.
AI.result: A scale-dependent, momentum-interpolated GUP effective metric is obtained, matching RG metric form but with γ̂ = γ̂(β₀); it yields improved black hole thermodynamics (e.g., corrected Hawking temperature, entropy) and more accurate shadow radius predictions compared to heuristic or earlier GUP metrics; exhibits agreement with certain quantum black hole models in limiting regimes; suggests a formal link to f(R) gravity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed metric provides a more physically motivated and phenomenologically robust realization of GUP-induced spacetime deformation, unifying experimental input (COW, photon box) with theoretical constraints (RG structure, black hole physics), and opens a pathway toward embedding GUP in extended gravitational theories like f(R) gravity.

title: Quantum Effects in Supersymmetric Galilean Yang-Mills
summary: We study the quantum dynamics of supersymmetric Galilean Yang-Mills (SGYM), with a focus on three dimensions where there is a classical scale symmetry. This is believed to be the worldvolume theory describing D2-branes within type IIA non-relativistic string theory and arises as a non-relativistic limit of maximally supersymmetric (relativistic) Yang-Mills. Unlike the relativistic case, we find that SGYM only admits perturbative dynamical excitations on the Coulomb branch. We show that in three dimensions the classical scale symmetry is broken at one-loop due to logarithmic divergences. These cannot be regulated without introducing additional marginal deformations, and we present evidence that the theory is asymptotically free once these are included. In particular our analysis suggests that three-dimensional SGYM flows to a strongly coupled non-relativistic M2-brane theory.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes quantum dynamics of 3D supersymmetric Galilean Yang-Mills (SGYM), finding perturbative excitations only on the Coulomb branch, one-loop breaking of classical scale symmetry due to logarithmic divergences, necessity of marginal deformations for regularization, asymptotic freedom upon inclusion of such deformations, and a flow to a strongly coupled non-relativistic M2-brane theory.
AI.motivation: To understand the quantum behavior of SGYM as the worldvolume theory of D2-branes in non-relativistic type IIA string theory and its relation to relativistic SYM via non-relativistic limit.
AI.method: Perturbative quantum field theory analysis, focusing on renormalization, symmetry breaking, and RG flow in three-dimensional SGYM; examination of Coulomb branch dynamics and logarithmic UV divergences.
AI.result: SGYM admits only perturbative dynamical excitations on the Coulomb branch; classical scale symmetry is broken at one-loop by logarithmic divergences; consistent regularization requires marginal deformations; theory becomes asymptotically free with them; flows to a strongly coupled non-relativistic M2-brane theory.
AI.conclusion: Three-dimensional SGYM is not UV-complete as originally formulated; its quantum consistency necessitates marginal deformations, leading to asymptotic freedom and an IR fixed point identified with a strongly coupled non-relativistic M2-brane theory.

title: Multi-scattering processes and spectral properties of low-energy QCD
summary: We compute quark and meson spectral functions in low-energy QCD, including all-order scatterings and decays of pions and the scalar $σ$-mode. For low energies the gluons decouple and the dynamics of two-flavour QCD is well-described by a Quark-Meson model. The computations are performed directly in Minkowski space, using the spectral functional renormalisation group. The full mesonic realtime dynamics is captured with the emergent composite approach which is extended here to realtime processes. The inclusion of all-order scatterings and decays is achieved through the self-consistent treatment of the scattering tails and the momentum-dependent resummation of the four-meson vertex via its Bethe-Salpeter equation. We illustrate the importance of higher-order scatterings using the example of the $π\to 3π$ scattering threshold - the lowest kinematically accessible channel for the pion.

AI.tldr: This paper computes quark and meson spectral functions in low-energy QCD using the spectral functional renormalisation group in Minkowski space, incorporating all-order scatterings and decays—including π→3π—via a self-consistent treatment of scattering tails and Bethe-Salpeter resummation of the four-meson vertex.
AI.motivation: To accurately describe real-time dynamics and spectral properties of light hadrons in low-energy QCD, where gluonic degrees of freedom decouple and chiral effective theories (e.g., Quark-Meson model) become appropriate, while going beyond standard perturbative or static approximations.
AI.method: Spectral functional renormalisation group (spectral FRG) formulated directly in Minkowski space; emergent composite approach extended to real-time processes; self-consistent inclusion of scattering tails; momentum-dependent resummation of the four-meson vertex via its Bethe-Salpeter equation.
AI.result: Full real-time spectral functions for quarks and mesons (including pions and σ-mode) are obtained, with quantitative demonstration that higher-order scatterings—particularly near the π→3π threshold—significantly modify spectral shapes and decay dynamics.
AI.conclusion: All-order scattering and decay effects are essential for accurate spectral functions in low-energy QCD; the spectral FRG with emergent composites and Bethe-Salpeter resummation provides a consistent, non-perturbative framework for real-time hadronic dynamics.

title: Duru-Kleinert Path Integral in Unimodular Quantum Cosmology
summary: The Wheeler-DeWitt equation of a flat Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker universe filled with pressureless dust and a cosmological constant in the unimodular gravity is recently shown to be equivalent to the radial Schrödinger equation of a hydrogen atom. In this paper, we revisit this correspondence between the unimodular quantum cosmology and the hydrogen atom by using the Duru-Kleinert path integration technique. The Duru-Kleinert time reparametrization transforms the Euclidean path integral of the universe into that of a one-dimensional Coulomb system. Through a Mellin-Barnes integral representation, we extract the bound state poles of the Green's function, which give the quantized negative cosmological constant. We compute the quantum tunneling rate from ``nothing'' to a universe directly within the Coulomb model. Furthermore, for a positive cosmological constant, we compute the spectral density and the Krylov complexity for the unbounded state.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes and explores a quantum mechanical analogy between unimodular quantum cosmology (for a flat FLRW universe with dust and Λ) and the hydrogen atom, using Duru-Kleinert path integration to map the cosmological path integral onto a 1D Coulomb system; it derives quantized negative Λ from bound-state poles, computes tunneling-from-nothing in that framework, and analyzes spectral density and Krylov complexity for positive Λ unbounded states.
AI.motivation: To deepen the recently discovered equivalence between the Wheeler-DeWitt equation in unimodular gravity and the hydrogen atom Schrödinger equation, and to exploit this correspondence—via advanced path integral methods—to extract physical quantum cosmological predictions (e.g., Λ quantization, tunneling rates, complexity) not readily accessible in standard approaches.
AI.method: Duru-Kleinert time reparametrization applied to the Euclidean path integral of the universe; mapping to a one-dimensional Coulomb system; Mellin-Barnes integral representation of the Green's function to identify bound-state poles; computation of quantum tunneling amplitude from 'nothing'; spectral analysis and Krylov complexity calculation for scattering (unbounded) states with positive Λ.
AI.result: Quantization condition for negative cosmological constant Λ derived from bound-state poles; explicit computation of the tunneling rate from 'nothing' to a classical universe within the Coulomb model; derivation of spectral density and Krylov complexity for the continuous spectrum associated with positive Λ.
AI.conclusion: The hydrogen atom correspondence is robust and computationally powerful: it yields concrete, testable quantum gravitational predictions—including discrete Λ spectra and dynamical complexity measures—in a simplified but physically relevant cosmological setting, supporting unimodular gravity as a viable framework for quantum cosmology.

title: Non-abelian uni-vector deformations in gauged supergravities and non-abelian Einstein-Maxwell theories
summary: We construct non-abelian uni-vector deformations of solutions in non-abelian Einstein\--Maxwell theories and gauged supergravities, obtained as Scherk--Schwarz reductions of general relativity and double field theory, respectively. We provide examples of deformed backgrounds for both cases. We show that non-abelian deformations in Einstein--Maxwell theories can be presented as coordinate transformations in the parent theory, general relativity, extending the result of arXiv:2508.09637 for abelian uni-vector deformations.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs non-abelian uni-vector deformations of solutions in non-abelian Einstein–Maxwell theories and gauged supergravities, showing they arise from Scherk–Schwarz reductions and can be interpreted as coordinate transformations in the parent GR theory.
AI.motivation: To generalize abelian uni-vector deformations to the non-abelian case and clarify their geometric origin in parent theories like general relativity and double field theory.
AI.method: Constructs non-abelian uni-vector deformations via Scherk–Schwarz reductions of general relativity and double field theory; analyzes deformed backgrounds and interprets deformations as coordinate transformations in the higher-dimensional parent theory.
AI.result: Non-abelian uni-vector deformations are explicitly constructed for Einstein–Maxwell and gauged supergravity contexts; crucially, such deformations in Einstein–Maxwell theories are shown to correspond to coordinate transformations in the unreduced general relativity framework.
AI.conclusion: Non-abelian uni-vector deformations retain a geometric interpretation as diffeomorphisms in the parent theory—extending the abelian case—and thus preserve underlying consistency with fundamental gravitational principles.

title: Localized scalar modes of $O(3)$ critical bubbles: partial-wave continuum mergers and wave-function deformation
summary: At phase coexistence, a degenerate quartic scalar potential admits an exact planar kink whose normal fluctuation operator is the modified Pöschl--Teller operator, with translational and positive shape states below a continuum beginning at $Λ=4$. We continue the two connected spectral bands through finite supercooling in a smooth one-component quartic benchmark and resolve $\ell=0,1,2$. The $O(3)$ bounce is obtained by singular collocation, while the radial Euclidean Hessian is analyzed by finite-difference diagonalization and independent threshold shooting. The positive $\ell=2$ and $\ell=1$ branches reach the common false-vacuum continuum threshold at $δ_{{\rm merge},2}=0.0900472$ and $δ_{{\rm merge},1}=0.1410162$, respectively. At each endpoint, $u_\ell\proptoρ^{-\ell}$ is square integrable and defines a threshold eigenstate; beyond the endpoint, however, no normalizable eigenstate continuation exists for the corresponding branch. The $\ell=0$ shape state remains bound up to the geometric wall crossover. Its planar-mode overlap, radial centroid, and distinct interior and exterior decay lengths reveal asymmetric wave-function deformation. Thus, angular spectral dissolution and the later geometric loss of a true-vacuum-like core are separate phenomena, revealing two distinct finite-supercooling fates of the planar shape mode.

AI.tldr: This paper studies spectral evolution of normal fluctuations around kink and bounce solutions in a quartic scalar field theory across phase coexistence and finite supercooling, focusing on angular momentum channels ℓ=0,1,2; it identifies threshold eigenstates at critical supercooling values where ℓ=1,2 branches merge into the continuum, while the ℓ=0 shape mode remains bound until geometric wall effects dominate.
AI.motivation: To understand how planar kink shape modes evolve under supercooling and whether they persist as bound states or dissolve into the continuum—key for vacuum decay dynamics and metastability in scalar field theories.
AI.method: Analytic continuation of spectral bands from the exactly solvable coexistence limit; singular collocation for the O(3) bounce; finite-difference diagonalization and threshold shooting for the radial Euclidean Hessian; analysis of ℓ=0,1,2 fluctuation spectra.
AI.result: ℓ=1 and ℓ=2 positive shape branches terminate at precise supercooling thresholds (δ_merge,1 ≈ 0.1410, δ_merge,2 ≈ 0.0900) as square-integrable threshold eigenstates u_ℓ ∝ ρ⁻ℓ; beyond these, no normalizable continuation exists; ℓ=0 remains bound up to geometric wall crossover, exhibiting asymmetric wavefunction deformation with distinct interior/exterior decay lengths.
AI.conclusion: Angular spectral dissolution (ℓ≥1) and geometric core loss (ℓ=0) are distinct mechanisms governing finite-supercooling fate of planar shape modes—implying two qualitatively different regimes for bubble nucleation and fluctuation stability.

title: Notes on Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson Spacetime
summary: The surface $r=\infty$ of the Kerr--Bertotti--Robinson (KBR) spacetime is not the collection of the endpoints of infinitely extended light rays, and the Coulomb type component of gravitational field strength represented by $Ψ_2$ remains nonvanishing there, indicating that this surface is not a real boundary. We construct a natural extension across this surface, which connects the exterior of one KBR region to the interior of a neighboring one and, upon iteration, produces an infinite chain of regions connected by wormhole-like bridges. The extension also exposes the neighboring ring singularity without an intervening horizon, challenging the weak cosmic censorship conjecture and raising the question of whether the extended geometry is stable under perturbations. We therefore study the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a test massless scalar field on a two-universe scattering segment. For axisymmetric perturbations, the existence of purely imaginary unstable QNMs is analytically proved for every $\ell$, with their origin tied to the chronology-violating region. In the $(\ell,m)=(2,2)$ sector, unstable QNM branches driven by a black-hole-bomb mechanism are found. Finally, the wormhole geometry produces a double-barrier cavity and families of weakly damped QNMs, suggesting echo-like responses.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the Kerr--Bertotti--Robinson (KBR) spacetime, showing that its r=∞ surface is not a true boundary but admits a smooth extension forming an infinite chain of universes connected by wormhole-like bridges; this extension exposes naked ring singularities, challenging weak cosmic censorship, and stability analysis via quasinormal modes reveals both chronology-driven instabilities and echo-producing double-barrier structures.
AI.motivation: To investigate the physical nature of the r=∞ surface in the KBR spacetime, test whether it constitutes a genuine boundary or can be extended, assess implications for cosmic censorship, and determine linear stability of the extended geometry against scalar perturbations.
AI.method: Geometric extension of the KBR metric across r=∞; analysis of Weyl scalar Ψ₂ to characterize gravitational field behavior; construction of a two-universe scattering segment; analytical and numerical study of quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a massless scalar field, including separation of axisymmetric (ℓ-dependent) and non-axisymmetric (ℓ,m)=(2,2) sectors; identification of instability mechanisms (chronology violation, black-hole-bomb).
AI.result: 1) The r=∞ surface is regular and extendable, yielding an infinite chain of causally disconnected KBR regions linked by traversable wormhole bridges; 2) The extension exposes naked ring singularities, violating weak cosmic censorship; 3) Axisymmetric QNMs possess purely imaginary unstable modes for all ℓ, rooted in chronology violation; 4) In the (ℓ,m)=(2,2) sector, black-hole-bomb–driven instabilities emerge; 5) The wormhole’s double-barrier potential supports families of weakly damped QNMs—potential sources of gravitational echoes.
AI.conclusion: The KBR spacetime admits a physically meaningful analytic extension beyond r=∞, resulting in a multiverse-like structure with observable instability signatures; its violation of weak cosmic censorship and presence of chronology-related and bomb-type instabilities imply nonlinear instability, undermining its viability as a realistic astrophysical model—though its QNM spectrum offers testable phenomenology (e.g., echoes) for exotic compact objects.

title: Quantum State of the Asymptotic Gravity Field from BRST Quantization
summary: We derive the quantum state of the asymptotic linearized gravity field of a compact energy source, using BRST quantization. Barnich has previously derived the quantum state of the U(1) field in QED using the Gauss law constraint. The role of Gauss's law is now played by the linearized Hamiltonian and momentum constraints in gravity. For a static mass source, only the scalar Hamiltonian constraint is shifted. The quantum state corresponding to the static Newton field originates in the non-radiative scalar constraint sector, not in the propagating transverse-traceless graviton sector. We discuss implications for holography and for black hole information: 1. the exact quantum state of the compact source is encoded in the asymptotic quantum state of its gravity field 2. Hawking amplitudes are dependent, via the gravity state outside the horizon, on the black hole internal state.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the quantum state of the asymptotic linearized gravity field of a compact source using BRST quantization, showing that the Newtonian field arises from the non-radiative scalar constraint sector—not the TT graviton sector—and argues that the full quantum state of a black hole is encoded in its asymptotic gravitational field, affecting Hawking radiation and holography.
AI.motivation: To understand how the quantum state of a compact energy source is encoded in its asymptotic gravitational field, especially in light of holography and the black hole information paradox; motivated by Barnich’s analogous QED treatment using Gauss law constraints.
AI.method: BRST quantization of linearized gravity; imposition of linearized Hamiltonian and momentum constraints as analogues of Gauss law; analysis of constraint sectors (scalar vs. transverse-traceless) for static mass sources.
AI.result: The quantum state of the static Newtonian gravitational field emerges exclusively from the non-radiative scalar (Hamiltonian) constraint sector; the asymptotic gravity field fully encodes the exact quantum state of the compact source; Hawking amplitudes depend on the black hole’s internal state through the external gravity state.
AI.conclusion: The asymptotic quantum gravity field—governed by constraints, not radiation—carries complete information about the source, supporting holographic encoding and challenging purely thermal interpretations of Hawking radiation.

title: Triangle Feynman diagram in the timelike region
summary: In Quantum Field Theory, triangle Feynman diagram $F(p_1^2,p_2^2,p_3^2|m_1,m_2,m_3)$ is an analytic function of its variables, whose analytic structure is fully determined by the location of singularities of the propagators of particles in the loop. The form factor $F(p_1^2,p_2^2,p_3^2|m_1,m_2,m_3)$ is easily calculable in the Euclidean region of all variables, $p_i^2<0$, $i=1,2,3$. A rigorous way to obtain the form factor in the timelike region is to perform the analytic continuation from the Euclidean region using single or double dispersion representations. On the other hand, there is a simple representation of the triangle as integral over Feynman parameters. The goal of this paper is to demonstrate that all known rigorous results of dispersion representations in the regions where some of the variables $p_i^2$ are in the physical Minkowski region, are reproduced by the Feynman-parameter representation for $F(p_1^2,p_2^2,p_3^2|m_1,m_2,m_3)$ by a mere replacement $p_i^2\to p_i^2+i0$ and $m_i^2\to m_i^2-i0$, where $m_i$ are masses of particles propagating in the loop. This simple replacement takes properly into account all subtle contributions given in the context of dispersion representations by the anomalous cuts and thresholds.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that the Feynman-parameter representation of the triangle diagram, with standard $i0$ prescriptions ($p_i^2 	o p_i^2 + i0$, $m_i^2 	o m_i^2 - i0$), rigorously reproduces all known dispersion-theoretic results—including anomalous cuts and thresholds—in physical (timelike/Minkowski) kinematic regions.
AI.motivation: To provide a simpler, unified derivation of the analytic structure of the triangle diagram in physical regions, bypassing the technical complexity of explicit dispersion representations while recovering their full rigor—including anomalous thresholds and cuts.
AI.method: Systematic application of the Feynman-parameter integral representation of the triangle diagram, combined with the standard causal $i\epsilon$ prescription for momenta and masses, followed by comparison with established single/double dispersion relations and their branch-cut structures.
AI.result: The $i0$-prescribed Feynman-parameter representation correctly yields the discontinuities, spectral functions, and analytic continuation across all physical regions—including cases with one or two timelike $p_i^2$—matching dispersion-theoretic predictions exactly, including contributions from anomalous cuts and thresholds.
AI.conclusion: The Feynman-parameter representation, augmented only by the conventional causal $i0$ prescription, is fully equivalent to rigorous dispersion analysis for the triangle diagram; it automatically encodes the complete singularity structure without requiring ad hoc treatment of anomalous thresholds.

title: On entropic cosmology, late time acceleration and the quantum bounce
summary: In this work, we present a unified entropic description of the quantum bounce that is present in Loop Quantum Cosmology (LQG) and dark energy that drives the late time acceleration of the Universe. By considering a minimal area $A_0$ for the Universe and a modified entropy area constructed as the sum of $S_Q$, $S_{BH}$ and $S_{DE}$, we derive the Friedmann equations. We show that in the limit $A\sim A_0$, there is a critical density that generates the quantum bounce and depends on the minimal area. Moreover, in the limit $A\gg A_0$ (large Universe) the late time dynamics gives an accelerating scale factor. Therefore, we can argue an entropic origin for the quantum bounce and dark energy.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified entropic framework linking the quantum bounce in Loop Quantum Cosmology and dark energy-driven cosmic acceleration via a modified entropy-area relation involving minimal area $A_0$.
AI.motivation: To unify two seemingly distinct cosmological phenomena—quantum bounce (from LQG) and late-time cosmic acceleration (attributed to dark energy)—under a common entropic origin, avoiding ad hoc energy components.
AI.method: Constructs a modified total entropy $S = S_Q + S_{BH} + S_{DE}$ based on a minimal fundamental area $A_0$, and derives Friedmann equations from thermodynamic first law applied to the apparent horizon using this entropy-area relation.
AI.result: Derives critical density for quantum bounce when $A \sim A_0$, and recovers accelerated expansion when $A \gg A_0$; both behaviors emerge naturally from the same entropic ansatz without introducing exotic matter fields.
AI.conclusion: Quantum bounce and dark energy can be simultaneously explained as thermodynamic consequences of quantum geometry-induced entropy modifications, supporting an emergent gravity paradigm in early- and late-time cosmology.

title: Non-invertible symmetry and vertex operator algebra outer-automorphism
summary: We argue that the non-invertible symmetry of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, obtained by combining S-duality, half-space gauging, and R-symmetry twist, is realized as an outer-automorphism of the associated vertex operator algebra. Hence, the Schur and Macdonald index of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory with non-invertible symmetry twist corresponds to the (refined) vacuum character of the associated vertex operator algebra with the outer-automorphism twist. We provide a few checks of our proposal from the large-$N$ limit and by matching the fusion rules, which involve charge conjugation on local operators. The `charged' Schur index indeed matches the outer-automorphism-twisted vacuum character.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that the non-invertible symmetry in N=4 super Yang-Mills, constructed from S-duality, half-space gauging, and R-symmetry twist, is realized as an outer-automorphism of its associated vertex operator algebra (VOA); consequently, the Schur and Macdonald indices under this twist equal the (refined) vacuum character of the VOA twisted by that outer-automorphism — verified via large-N limits and fusion rule consistency including charge conjugation.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical realization and algebraic structure of non-invertible symmetries in 4d N=4 super Yang-Mills, particularly how they manifest in protected sectors (Schur/Macdonald indices) and connect to VOA representation theory.
AI.method: Combines S-duality, half-space gauging, and R-symmetry twist to construct a non-invertible symmetry; identifies it with an outer-automorphism of the associated VOA; computes and compares twisted vacuum characters against the 'charged' Schur index and fusion rules involving charge conjugation.
AI.result: The Schur and Macdonald indices with non-invertible symmetry twist match the (refined) outer-automorphism-twisted vacuum character of the VOA; consistency confirmed in the large-N limit and via fusion rule matching—including charge conjugation of local operators.
AI.conclusion: Non-invertible symmetries in N=4 SYM are concretely realized as outer-automorphisms of its chiral algebra (VOA), and their protected indices are encoded in twisted vacuum characters—establishing a precise bridge between higher-categorical symmetries and VOA representation theory.

title: Perturbative Hairy Black Branes in the $G_{2}$-Invariant Sector of Dyonic ISO(7) Gauged Supergravity
summary: We construct perturbative black-brane solutions carrying neutral scalar hair in the $G_{2}$-invariant truncation of four-dimensional dyonic $\mathcal{N}=8$ ISO(7) gauged supergravity, an exact consistent truncation of massive type~IIA supergravity on $S^{6}$. Expanding around the $G_{2}$-symmetric AdS$_{4}$-Schwarzschild black brane in powers of a dimensionless scalar-charge parameter $\eps$, we show that the perturbation hierarchy reduces, order by order, to a nested sequence of inhomogeneous Legendre equations (demonstrated through second order). The first-order scalar satisfies a Pöschl--Teller equation with exact parameter $ν(ν+1)=2/3$, giving $ν=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{33}}{6}$, and the first-order metric is fixed algebraically by the same function, $A^{(1)}=-\tfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}φ^{(1)}$, so the entire $\mathcal{O}(\eps)$ sector is one Legendre function. An identity $ν+1=Δ_{+}/3$, with $Δ_{+}=(3+\sqrt{33})/2\approx 4.372$ the conformal dimension of the dual scalar operator, relates the Pöschl-Teller parameter to the AdS/CFT dictionary via the nonlinear Fefferman-Graham map $z \propto z_{\mathrm{FG}}^{3}$. The $\mathcal{O}(\eps^{2})$ back-reaction yields explicit corrections to the renormalized free energy and Bekenstein-Hawking entropy density at fixed temperature, consistent with the first law; equivalently, at fixed entropy or energy density it \emph{lowers} the Hawking temperature by $δT/T=\mathcal{O}(\eps^{2})$. For the leading transport coefficients the shear viscosity saturates $η/s=1/(4π)$, while the Eling-Oz horizon formula gives a nonzero bulk viscosity $ζ/η=\bigl(\tfrac{Δ_{+}-3}{2}\bigr)^{2}\eps^{2}=\tfrac{3(7-\sqrt{33})}{8}\eps^{2}\approx0.471\,\eps^{2}$. With $c_{s}^{2}=\tfrac12-\mathcal O(\eps^{2})<\tfrac12$, this indicates a softening of the equation of state.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs perturbative black-brane solutions with neutral scalar hair in a G₂-invariant truncation of 4D N=8 ISO(7) gauged supergravity, deriving analytic scalar and metric perturbations via Legendre and Pöschl–Teller equations; it computes second-order thermodynamic and transport corrections—including entropy decrease, temperature lowering at fixed entropy/energy, η/s saturation, nonzero bulk viscosity ζ/η ∝ ε², and sound speed softening—consistent with AdS/CFT and the first law.
AI.motivation: To systematically construct and characterize black-brane solutions with neutral scalar hair in a controlled, holographically dual setting—specifically the G₂-invariant truncation of 4D N=8 ISO(7) gauged supergravity—which admits an exact embedding into massive IIA on S⁶, enabling precise AdS/CFT interpretation of scalar hair and its thermodynamic/transport consequences.
AI.method: Perturbative expansion in a dimensionless scalar-charge parameter ε around the G₂-symmetric AdS₄-Schwarzschild black brane; reduction of field equations order-by-order to inhomogeneous Legendre equations; exact solution of the first-order scalar perturbation via a Pöschl–Teller equation with ν(ν+1)=2/3; algebraic determination of first-order metric; nonlinear Fefferman–Graham map to relate bulk ν to boundary conformal dimension Δ₊; computation of renormalized free energy, entropy density, Hawking temperature shift, shear and bulk viscosities (via Eling–Oz horizon formula), and speed of sound.
AI.result: First-order solution fully determined by one Legendre function; ν linked to Δ₊ via ν+1 = Δ₊/3; O(ε²) backreaction yields explicit negative corrections to entropy density at fixed T, and lowers T at fixed s or ε; η/s = 1/(4π) remains saturated; nonzero bulk viscosity ζ/η = ((Δ₊−3)/2)² ε² ≈ 0.471 ε²; sound speed squared cₛ² = ½ − O(ε²), indicating softening of the equation of state.
AI.conclusion: Neutral scalar hair induces controlled, calculable deviations from the universal hydrodynamic predictions of Einstein gravity: while shear viscosity retains its universal value, bulk viscosity emerges quadratically in scalar charge, and thermodynamics exhibits nontrivial corrections consistent with the first law and AdS/CFT—signaling a physically softer, more compressible dual fluid.

title: Classical and Quantum Chaos from Foundations to Holography
summary: These notes develop the diagnostics of chaos from their classical definitions through to holography, in six lectures given at the ST4 Workshop, Chennai Mathematical Institute, in 2026. No prior exposure to chaos theory is assumed. Lectures 1 and 2 define classical chaos geometrically and build the instruments that measure it, every one of which reads a phase-space trajectory. Quantization removes that trajectory, and Lectures 3 and 4 rebuild the instruments from spectra and eigenstates instead: level statistics, random matrix theory, the spectral form factor and eigenstate thermalization, as much the working toolkit for thermalization in many-body physics as for holography. What they return is a classification and a count rather than a rate. Lecture 5 recovers the rate from the squared commutator, treats scrambling as operator growth, follows the commutator to the out-of-time-order correlator, marks where that diagnostic stops being reliable, and reaches the butterfly velocity and the chaos bound. Lecture 6 constructs the eternal black hole, the thermofield double and the shock-wave geometry behind that bound, then follows two probes whose exponents discriminate between backgrounds where the horizon result cannot, one tracking a thermodynamic phase transition, the other resolving an anisotropy induced by a background field. Every lecture closes with exercises. Claude Opus 5, an AI assistant developed by Anthropic, worked as a research assistant under the author's direction.

AI.tldr: A six-lecture pedagogical series bridging classical chaos diagnostics (e.g., Lyapunov exponents via phase-space trajectories) to quantum and holographic diagnostics (e.g., OTOCs, spectral form factor, ETH), culminating in black hole geometry and refined chaos probes distinguishing horizon-degenerate backgrounds.
AI.motivation: To systematically develop chaos diagnostics from classical mechanics through quantum many-body physics to AdS/CFT holography, making them accessible without prior chaos background and unifying geometric, spectral, and operator-based measures.
AI.method: Pedagogical lecture format progressing from geometric definitions of chaos (Lectures 1–2), to quantum spectral tools (Lectures 3–4: level statistics, RMT, SFF, ETH), to operator growth and OTOCs (Lecture 5), and finally to holographic constructions (eternal black hole, TFD, shock waves) and refined dual probes (Lecture 6).
AI.result: A unified framework linking classical chaos measures to quantum thermalization diagnostics and holographic chaos bounds; introduces two new probe exponents that discriminate between black hole backgrounds indistinguishable by the standard Lyapunov exponent alone—e.g., detecting thermodynamic phase transitions or field-induced anisotropies.
AI.conclusion: Chaos diagnostics evolve from trajectory-based rates in classical systems to spectral classifications in quantum systems, and finally to operator scrambling and geometric probes in holography; the chaos bound and its saturation are contextualized within black hole microstructure, and refined probes extend diagnostic power beyond the universal butterfly velocity.

title: Three-body forces in the quark model
summary: We review the connection between constituent-quark Hamiltonians and QCD and investigate the long-standing difficulty of describing meson and baryon spectra with one common two-body interaction. A Hamiltonian calibrated to ground-state mesons leaves systematic baryon mass residuals, largest in the light-quark sector and decreasing toward heavier flavors. We show that a short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction substantially reduces this incompatibility. Mass-scaled finite-range profiles yield high-accuracy baryon spectra, whereas flavor-independent common-range profiles do not remove the residual flavor pattern. The result is tested on additional ground-state baryons outside the calibration set and through meson--baryon compatibility analyses across several alternative quark-model Hamiltonians. We also benchmark radial and orbital excitations to identify the regime in which a static compact valence Hamiltonian remains reliable, and provide explicit color-spin matrix elements for two- and three-body operators in baryons and multiquark configurations. Within the tested valence-space representations, the results indicate that a mass-dependent short-range connected three-quark interaction provides the missing contribution required for a consistent simultaneous description of meson and baryon ground-state spectra.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a systematic incompatibility between meson and baryon spectra when modeled with standard two-body constituent-quark Hamiltonians, and demonstrates that adding a mass-scaled, short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction resolves the discrepancy—enabling high-accuracy, simultaneous description of ground-state mesons and baryons.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing inconsistency in quark models where a single two-body interaction calibrated to meson spectra fails to reproduce baryon masses accurately—especially for light quarks—indicating missing physics beyond pairwise forces.
AI.method: Systematic analysis of residual mass discrepancies across meson and baryon ground states; introduction and calibration of a short-range, color-spin-dependent connected three-quark interaction; comparison of mass-scaled vs. flavor-independent finite-range profiles; validation via out-of-sample baryons, meson–baryon compatibility tests across multiple Hamiltonians, and benchmarking of radial/orbital excitations; explicit computation of color-spin matrix elements for two- and three-body operators in baryons and multiquark systems.
AI.result: A mass-scaled, short-range, connected three-quark interaction significantly reduces baryon mass residuals (especially for light quarks) without degrading meson fits; flavor-independent range profiles fail to eliminate the residual flavor pattern; the improvement holds across multiple Hamiltonians and generalizes to uncalibrated baryons; static valence Hamiltonians remain reliable only up to moderate orbital/radial excitations.
AI.conclusion: A mass-dependent short-range connected three-quark interaction is essential—and sufficient within the valence approximation—for a consistent, high-accuracy simultaneous description of meson and baryon ground-state spectra, resolving a fundamental limitation of conventional two-body quark models.

title: Maximal Enhancements in Eight-Dimensional Non-Supersymmetric Heterotic Strings
summary: We classify maximally enhanced, rank-preserving non-supersymmetric heterotic strings in eight dimensions by studying orbifolds of supersymmetric heterotic strings on $T^2$. We first review the construction in nine dimensions, where it reproduces the $95$ maximally semisimple enhancement points obtained from previous extended-Dynkin analyses. We then start from the maximally enhanced supersymmetric Narain points in eight dimensions and use Kac's theorem to enumerate candidate order-two inner actions, retaining only those that lift to consistent Narain-lattice shifts. This gives $1210$ maximal enhancement points, of which $71$ are tachyon-free, and $25$ have neither tachyons nor shifted-sector massless scalars. For each entry we determine the gauge algebra and the low-lying scalar and fermion spectra, and for the tachyon-free cases we evaluate the one-loop cosmological constant. For the 25 subcases without shifted-sector massless scalars, we further compute the Hessian of the one-loop potential and test the refined de Sitter swampland conjecture.

AI.tldr: This paper classifies maximally enhanced, rank-preserving, non-supersymmetric heterotic string vacua in eight dimensions via orbifold constructions from supersymmetric Narain lattices on $T^2$, identifying 1210 maximal enhancement points—71 tachyon-free, 25 with no shifted-sector massless scalars—and tests the refined de Sitter swampland conjecture via Hessian analysis of the one-loop potential.
AI.motivation: To systematically classify stable, phenomenologically viable non-supersymmetric heterotic string vacua in eight dimensions that preserve rank and maximize gauge enhancement, while probing quantum stability and swampland constraints.
AI.method: Orbifold construction of non-supersymmetric heterotic strings from supersymmetric Narain compactifications on $T^2$; application of Kac's theorem to enumerate order-two inner automorphisms; consistency checks via Narain-lattice shift lifting; spectral computation (gauge algebra, scalars, fermions); one-loop cosmological constant evaluation; Hessian analysis of the one-loop potential for swampland testing.
AI.result: 1210 maximal enhancement points classified; 71 tachyon-free; 25 free of both tachyons and shifted-sector massless scalars; full gauge algebras and low-energy spectra determined; one-loop cosmological constant computed for tachyon-free cases; Hessian analysis performed for the 25 cases, yielding quantitative tests of the refined de Sitter swampland conjecture.
AI.conclusion: The classification provides a complete census of rank-preserving, maximally enhanced non-supersymmetric heterotic vacua in $D=8$, revealing strong constraints from modular invariance and quantum stability; the Hessian results offer concrete evidence supporting (or delimiting) the refined de Sitter swampland conjecture in this controlled string context.

title: Quantum Magic in High Energy Collision
summary:
Quantum magic, or nonstabilizerness, is a quantum resource associated with computational advantage in quantum systems. In high energy collisions, Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) is inefficient at generating magic
  while the weak mixing angle, a fundamental constant of nature, sits near a value that minimizes magic production in charged-lepton scattering. These observations were made in the laboratory (lab) basis, in which spin is projected along the incoming beam axis. An alternative choice is the helicity basis, in which spin is projected along the direction of motion of each particle. The transformation between these two bases is, in general, not a Clifford operation and therefore can change the amount of magic. We present a detailed study of magic production in both bases for QED and electroweak processes, and compare these results with the basis-invariant non-local magic. In the ultra-relativistic limit, magic production is generally smaller in the helicity basis due to helicity selection rules, while the lab basis generally yields less magic in the non-relativistic regime. We provide circuit realizations of the ultra-relativistic Bhabha amplitudes using linear combinations of unitaries and show that the lab basis construction contains a larger $T$-gate count at generic scattering angles. Interestingly, in both bases the physical weak mixing angle lies close to the value that minimizes magic production.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quantum magic (nonstabilizerness) as a resource in high-energy QED and electroweak scattering, comparing its production in lab vs. helicity spin bases; it finds basis-dependent magic magnitudes—helicity suppresses magic ultra-relativistically due to selection rules, while lab basis suppresses it non-relativistically—and shows the physical weak mixing angle near-minimizes magic in both bases.
AI.motivation: To understand whether quantum magic—a resource linked to quantum computational advantage—is physically relevant in high-energy particle processes, and to assess how its quantification depends on the choice of spin basis (lab vs. helicity), especially given prior observations that the weak mixing angle coincides with a magic-minimizing value in the lab basis.
AI.method: Analytical and numerical computation of magic measures (e.g., stabilizer rank, robustness, or mana) for QED and electroweak scattering amplitudes in both lab and helicity bases; derivation of basis transformation properties with respect to Clifford group; circuit synthesis of ultra-relativistic Bhabha scattering amplitudes using linear combinations of unitaries (LCU); comparison with basis-invariant non-local magic measures.
AI.result: Magic production is reduced in the helicity basis in the ultra-relativistic limit due to helicity conservation/selection rules, whereas the lab basis yields lower magic in the non-relativistic regime; circuit implementations confirm higher T-gate counts in the lab basis for generic angles; the experimentally measured weak mixing angle remains near the magic-minimizing value in both bases.
AI.conclusion: Quantum magic in scattering processes is basis-sensitive but exhibits robust physical structure: its minimization at the physical weak mixing angle persists across spin bases, suggesting a potential deep connection between fundamental constants and quantum resource constraints in quantum field theory.
